rows.what_happened: The largest online service in the US went dark for about 19 hours.
rows.impact: About 6 million members cut off.
rows.cause: Routine maintenance that installed new software.

rows.what_happened: One small provider announced a large part of the internet's routing table as its own, and traffic for many networks was pulled into it.
rows.impact: Large parts of the internet unreachable.
rows.cause: A customer's full routing view was re-announced without AS path or prefix filters.

rows.what_happened: A firmware upgrade on a switch card triggered software flaws that spread across the network.
rows.impact: Business customers off for six to 26 hours, among them thousands of card transaction customers.
rows.cause: Firmware upgrade procedure on a Cisco switch card.

rows.what_happened: The satellite lost attitude control, and US pager networks and several TV feeds went silent.
rows.impact: At least 40 million pager customers; the satellite carried about 90% of US pager transmissions (NASA).
rows.cause: The onboard control system and its backup switch failed.

rows.what_happened: A Word macro virus mailed itself on from each infected computer through Outlook.
rows.impact: Microsoft suspended outgoing email for about five hours; in his plea agreement the author admitted more than $80 million in damage.
rows.cause: Macro virus run by recipients opening an attached document.

rows.what_happened: The spacecraft was lost on arrival at Mars.
rows.impact: Mission lost.
rows.cause: One ground software team used English units and the other metric for a navigation value.

rows.what_happened: Faults in the Horizon accounting software showed false shortfalls. Many postmasters were pursued, and some convicted, for losses that did not exist.
rows.impact: UK government: GBP 1,039 million paid in redress across the Horizon schemes, as of 9 June 2025.
rows.cause: Software faults in the Horizon system (start date approximate; see report).

rows.what_happened: Software everywhere stored the year in two digits, so 2000 could be read as 1900.
rows.impact: About $308 billion spent on fixes worldwide (Computerworld), more than $100 billion in the US (Commerce Department); no major failures at the rollover.
rows.cause: Two-digit year fields in old code and data.

rows.what_happened: Denial-of-service floods took down the largest commercial sites of the day over several days.
rows.impact: Yahoo down for almost an hour; a 15-year-old in Montreal was later sentenced for the attacks.
rows.cause: Distributed denial of service from compromised machines.

rows.what_happened: A script worm arrived as a love letter and mailed itself to everyone in the Outlook address book.
rows.impact: More than 420,000 hosts reported to CERT-CC on the first day (GAO); damage estimates from $100 million to over $10 billion.
rows.cause: Users opened LOVE-LETTER-FOR-YOU.TXT.vbs, which ran as a script because Windows hid the .vbs extension.

rows.what_happened: A worm spread through a buffer overflow in Microsoft's IIS web server.
rows.impact: 359,000 hosts infected in under 14 hours (CAIDA). The patch, MS01-033, had been out since 18 June 2001.
rows.cause: Unpatched servers.

rows.what_happened: A worm spread to Windows servers and desktops by five routes at once: email, open network shares, infected web pages, holes in IIS and back doors left by Code Red.
rows.impact: Windows machines worldwide. CERT warned the same day (CA-2001-26).
rows.cause: Known holes and open shares on Windows machines.

rows.what_happened: A worm spread through a buffer overrun in SQL Server 2000 and its desktop engine.
rows.impact: At least 75,000 hosts; more than 90% of vulnerable hosts infected within 10 minutes (CAIDA). The patch, MS02-039, had been out since 24 July 2002.
rows.cause: Unpatched servers.

rows.what_happened: A worm spread through a hole in the Windows RPC service and made infected machines reboot.
rows.impact: The patch, MS03-026, had been out since 16 July 2003.
rows.cause: Unpatched Windows machines.

rows.what_happened: The alarm system at FirstEnergy failed, operators did not see lines tripping, and the failure cascaded across the grid.
rows.impact: 50 million people and 61,800 MW of load; US cost $4 to $10 billion (US-Canada Task Force).
rows.cause: A software failure in the alarm processing of the control room system, plus tree contact and operators who did not know the alarms were dead.

rows.what_happened: An email worm spread faster than any before it, and infected machines then flooded SCO's website, and in a later variant Microsoft's.
rows.impact: About 500,000 computers infected.
rows.cause: An email attachment that people opened.

rows.what_happened: A worm spread between Windows machines with no one clicking anything. Delta cancelled flights and UK coastguard systems went down for hours. A German 18-year-old was arrested in May.
rows.impact: Flights cancelled, coastguard and other systems down for hours.
rows.cause: A Windows hole Microsoft had patched on 13 April 2004.

rows.what_happened: The airline's crew scheduling system stopped on Christmas Day.
rows.impact: All 1,100 Comair flights cancelled; about 269,000 passengers affected between 22 and 28 December.
rows.cause: Storm changes hit a fixed limit of 32,000 trip transactions a month that neither the airline nor the vendor knew existed.

rows.what_happened: Intruders took payment card data from the retailer's systems; disclosed in January 2007.
rows.impact: About 45.7 million card numbers (company 10-K).
rows.cause: Network intrusion.

rows.what_happened: Denial-of-service floods hit government, bank and newspaper sites after a Soviet war memorial was moved in Tallinn.
rows.impact: About three weeks; some sites blocked access from outside Estonia to stay up.
rows.cause: Botnet denial of service.

rows.organisation_system: US Customs and Border Protection at LAX
rows.what_happened: The system that clears arriving international passengers went down.
rows.impact: About 18,000 passengers waited for clearance, some for hours on the tarmac (NPR).
rows.cause: Hardware fault in the customs computer system.

rows.what_happened: The peer-to-peer network collapsed after millions of computers rebooted at once for Windows Update.
rows.impact: Skype was unavailable to the majority of its users for about two days.
rows.cause: A flood of log-ins met a previously unseen bug in the network's resource allocation, which stopped it from healing itself.

rows.what_happened: GitHub officially opens after its beta, and the code becomes a social platform.
The random number generator in Debian's openssl package was predictable, so keys could be guessed.
rows.impact: Only Debian's openssl package from 0.9.8c-1 (uploaded 17 Sep 2006; etch, testing, unstable; sarge not affected). Affected keys had to be regenerated.
rows.cause: Mistaken Debian-specific change to the openssl package.

rows.what_happened: Compute rental becomes a production service with a 99.95% availability SLA.
A worm spread through a hole in the Windows Server service, network shares and USB drives.
rows.impact: F-Secure estimated more than 9 million infected PCs in January 2009. The patch, MS08-067, had been out since 23 October 2008.
rows.cause: Unpatched machines and weak passwords.

rows.what_happened: Patrick Debois organises the first DevOpsDays and, by his own account, accidentally gives the movement its name.

rows.organisation_system: Google and at least 20 companies (Operation Aurora)
rows.what_happened: A targeted attack from China on Google's corporate infrastructure to steal intellectual property.
rows.impact: Google said at least 20 other large companies were also attacked.
rows.cause: Targeted APT attack.

rows.what_happened: A worm exploiting a zero-day in Windows shortcut handling and USB spread to attack Siemens industrial control systems.
rows.impact: ICS-CERT's 2010 review calls it 'the first malware created specifically to target industrial control systems'.
rows.cause: A cyber weapon aimed at industrial control systems.

rows.what_happened: Intruders took account data between 17 and 19 April 2011, and Sony switched the services off.
rows.impact: About 77 million accounts; the network stayed down for more than three weeks.
rows.cause: Network intrusion.

rows.what_happened: A network change during planned maintenance triggered a re-mirroring storm in EBS.
rows.impact: Started 07:47 UTC (00:47 PDT) on 21 Apr. About 13% of volumes in the zone got stuck; 0.07% could not be restored in a consistent state.
rows.cause: Network error during a planned change, followed by a re-mirroring storm.

rows.what_happened: A deep convolutional network wins ImageNet, starting the deep learning era.
About 6.5 million LinkedIn password hashes were posted online. In 2016 the same breach turned out to cover far more accounts.
rows.impact: About 6.5 million passwords in 2012; more than 117 million accounts by 2016.
rows.cause: Intrusion into LinkedIn's systems; the passwords were stored as unsalted hashes.

rows.what_happened: An incomplete deployment to 1 of 8 servers woke old Power Peg code through a reused flag.
rows.impact: About 45 minutes; 4 million executions in 154 stocks (SEC order); loss above $460 million.
rows.cause: Power Peg unused since 2003 and broken by a 2005 change; manual deployment missed one server.

rows.what_happened: Theft of user account data in August 2013. Disclosed in December 2016 as more than 1 billion accounts; in October 2017 Yahoo said every account had been affected.
rows.impact: All Yahoo user accounts, reported as about 3 billion.
rows.cause: Not published in detail.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took customer records and part of the Photoshop source code.
rows.impact: About 38 million active users; the leaked file held about 152 million addresses.
rows.cause: Intrusion into Adobe's systems.

rows.what_happened: Unauthorised access to payment card data in US stores.
rows.impact: About 40 million payment cards, and personal data of up to 70 million customers; Target says the two groups overlap by at least 12 million. Breach window 27 Nov to 15 Dec 2013.
rows.cause: Point-of-sale malware; the attackers entered with network credentials stolen from an HVAC vendor (US Senate Commerce Committee report, 2014).

rows.what_happened: Server memory can be read through the TLS heartbeat extension.
rows.impact: Bug introduced Dec 2011, in releases from 14 Mar 2012, fixed 7 Apr 2014 (about 2 years in releases).
rows.cause: Missing bounds check.

rows.what_happened: Specially crafted environment variables could make Bash run commands.
rows.impact: US-CERT alert dated 25 Sep 2014.
rows.cause: Parsing error for functions in environment variables.

rows.what_happened: Attackers wiped computers across Sony Pictures' network and leaked its films, emails and staff data. The FBI blamed North Korea.
rows.impact: Hard drives across the company wiped.
rows.cause: Destructive malware.

rows.what_happened: A buffer overflow in glibc's gethostbyname functions could be triggered with a crafted hostname, so a remote attacker could take over a Linux server that used them.
rows.impact: Affects glibc-2.2 (released 10 Nov 2000) up to the fix of 21 May 2013, first shipped in glibc-2.18 (12 Aug 2013).
rows.cause: Buffer overflow in __nss_hostname_digits_dots(), reached through gethostbyname and gethostbyname2.

rows.what_happened: Attackers broke into a database of Anthem, the second-largest US health insurer.
rows.impact: 78.8 million people.
rows.cause: Intrusion into an IT system.

rows.what_happened: The largest DDoS attack on github.com up to that time.
rows.impact: Began about 02:00 UTC on 26 Mar 2015; still ongoing when GitHub posted on 27 Mar.
rows.cause: DDoS.

rows.what_happened: Theft of personnel records and of background-investigation records of US federal employees and applicants.
rows.impact: About 21.5 million people in background-investigation records and 4.2 million in personnel records.
rows.cause: Intrusion into OPM networks, found in April 2015.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took control of three Ukrainian power companies' systems and switched off power. The first known cyberattack to cut a power grid.
rows.impact: About 225,000 customers lost power.
rows.cause: Remote access to control systems, BlackEnergy malware.

rows.what_happened: The author unpublished 273 packages from npm, including left-pad; builds broke across the ecosystem.
rows.impact: Hundreds of failures per minute after 21:30 UTC (14:30 PDT); package restored.
rows.cause: No protection against removal of depended-on packages.

rows.what_happened: Users coordinated an attack that exploited Tay's learning, and the bot began posting offensive messages.
rows.impact: Microsoft took the bot offline within the first 24 hours.
rows.cause: A learning bot vulnerable to malicious input.

rows.what_happened: Seven autonomous systems find and patch vulnerabilities without humans (automated analysis, not LLMs).
A race condition in copy-on-write handling let a local user write to read-only memory and gain root.
rows.impact: Present since Linux 2.6.22 (2007), about nine years.
rows.cause: Race condition in the memory subsystem.

rows.what_happened: Two DDoS waves on the DNS provider made its customers' sites unreachable.
rows.impact: Waves 11:10 to 13:20 and 15:50 to 17:00 UTC; up to 100,000 malicious endpoints; retries 10 to 20 times normal.
rows.cause: IoT botnet Mirai using default passwords.

rows.what_happened: An engineer accidentally deleted primary database data; the backups had been failing unnoticed.
rows.impact: Lost from about 17:20 UTC on 31 Jan (postmortem gives the end as 00:00 or 23:30 UTC): about 5,000 projects, 5,000 comments, 700 accounts. Repositories not affected.
rows.cause: Manual operation on production; backups not verified.

rows.what_happened: An incorrect input to a playbook command removed more servers than intended.
rows.impact: 17:37 to 21:54 UTC (09:37 to 13:54 PST); cascade to other AWS services.
rows.cause: Manual command without safety limits.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware worm spread through an SMB vulnerability (MS17-010).
rows.impact: Europol: about 200,000 victims in at least 150 countries. In England 81 of 236 NHS trusts were hit and about 19,000 appointments cancelled (NAO). Microsoft's patch was released 14 Mar 2017, about two months before.
rows.cause: Unpatched systems.

rows.what_happened: A power supply at a data centre near Heathrow was disconnected; the surge on reconnection damaged IT systems.
rows.impact: About 75,000 passengers affected over a holiday weekend; IAG estimated the cost at GBP 58 million.
rows.cause: Human error on the power supply, per the airline.

rows.what_happened: The architecture behind modern large language models.
Destructive malware disguised as ransomware hit many countries and industries.
rows.impact: Effects in multiple countries and sectors (CISA); a White House assessment put the damage above $10 billion (Wired).
rows.cause: Malware (CISA says a Petya variant).

rows.what_happened: Consumer data was stolen through an unpatched Apache Struts flaw (CVE-2017-5638).
rows.impact: About 147 million people; the flaw went unpatched for more than 4 months.
rows.cause: Unpatched portal, no network segmentation, plain-text passwords.

rows.what_happened: A signed release of CCleaner, a popular cleanup tool, came with a backdoor built in.
rows.impact: About 2.27 million users installed it.
rows.cause: The vendor's build was tampered with before signing.

rows.what_happened: Researchers showed that a 1998 padding-oracle attack by Bleichenbacher still worked against many TLS servers that used RSA key exchange, and could impersonate a site such as Facebook with its certificate.
rows.impact: Almost a third of the top 100 domains in the Alexa list were affected, per the authors.
rows.cause: Old RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 padding check that many TLS stacks never fixed after the 1998 attack.

rows.what_happened: Amplification DDoS attack through memcached servers.
rows.impact: Peak 1.35 Tbit/s; unavailable 17:21 to 17:26 UTC, degraded until 17:30 UTC.
rows.cause: DDoS amplification.

rows.what_happened: Migration of customer accounts from Lloyds systems to a new core platform from its owner Sabadell failed on the switchover weekend.
rows.impact: Weeks of disruption to online and mobile banking; FCA and PRA fines totalling GBP 48.65 million in December 2022.
rows.cause: Regulators found the migration programme was not organised and controlled adequately.

rows.what_happened: A malicious dependency, flatmap-stream, targeting Copay wallets was added to a popular package.
rows.impact: Dependency added 9 Sep 2018; discovered 26 Nov 2018 (about 2.5 months).
rows.cause: Maintainer rights handed to an unknown party.

rows.what_happened: An attacker inside the Starwood guest reservation database since 2014 was found after Marriott had bought Starwood.
rows.impact: 339 million guest records worldwide, per the UK ICO; ICO fine GBP 18.4 million (2020).
rows.cause: Intrusion from 2014, undetected through the acquisition.

rows.what_happened: Two fatal 737 MAX crashes led to a worldwide grounding of the aircraft. Boeing later said the total cost would be more than USD 18 billion.
rows.impact: Company statement on 29 Jan 2020: total cost of the grounding, including restart of production, will surpass USD 18 billion.
rows.cause: Flight-control software (MCAS) built on wrong assumptions about pilot reaction, per Boeing's CEO.

rows.what_happened: Crafted TCP selective acknowledgements from a remote peer could crash a Linux server. Jonathan Looney of Netflix found it.
rows.impact: Every Linux kernel from 2.6.29, released in March 2009, about ten years.
rows.cause: An integer overflow in the kernel's SACK handling.

rows.what_happened: Customer and applicant data stored in the cloud was copied by an outsider.
rows.impact: About 100 million people in the US and 6 million in Canada.
rows.cause: A configuration vulnerability, per Capital One, reported by an outside researcher on 17 July 2019.

rows.what_happened: A 175 billion parameter language model learns new tasks from a few examples given in the prompt.
A backdoor in Orion updates; CISA issued Emergency Directive 21-01.
rows.impact: Federal agencies ordered to disconnect or shut down Orion. Fewer than 18,000 customers installed the bad update; SolarWinds later said fewer than 100 were actually hacked.
rows.cause: Compromise of the vendor's build pipeline.

rows.what_happened: A heap overflow in sudo let any local user gain root in the default configuration.
rows.impact: Introduced in July 2011, disclosed 26 January 2021, almost ten years.
rows.cause: Heap-based buffer overflow.

rows.what_happened: Data scraped from Facebook profiles through the contact importer before September 2019 was published free online.
rows.impact: Reported as more than 533 million users.
rows.cause: Scraping through a contact importer feature, fixed in 2019 per Facebook.

rows.what_happened: The uploader script was periodically altered and could export secrets from customers' CI environments.
rows.impact: Changes from 31 Jan 2021; fixed 1 Apr 2021; disclosed 15 Apr 2021.
rows.cause: Leaked Google Cloud Storage key, exposed by an error in Docker image creation.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware hit the company's IT network, and the company shut down its fuel pipeline on the US East Coast as a precaution.
rows.impact: Pipeline operations stopped; a ransom of USD 4.4 million was paid, of which the DOJ later seized about USD 2.3 million.
rows.cause: A legacy VPN account with single-factor authentication, per the CEO's testimony.

rows.what_happened: A valid customer configuration change triggered a latent bug that made 85% of the network return errors.
rows.impact: 09:47 to 12:35 UTC; most services recovered by 11:00 UTC.
rows.cause: Latent software defect in code deployed earlier.

rows.what_happened: The REvil ransomware group went through Kaseya's remote IT management software to the businesses that IT providers ran with it.
rows.impact: At least 60 Kaseya customers and about 1,500 businesses downstream.
rows.cause: A flaw in Kaseya VSA servers, used to push ransomware.

rows.what_happened: A heap out-of-bounds write in the netfilter x_tables code let a local user gain root, using a user namespace.
rows.impact: Linux kernels from about 2006 up to the 2021 fix; the writeup calls it a 15-year-old bug.
rows.cause: Out-of-bounds write in the x_tables compat path (xt_compat_target_from_user).

rows.what_happened: A configuration update hit a bug in Akamai's DNS service, and many large sites were unreachable.
rows.impact: Up to an hour.
rows.cause: A software configuration update that set off a bug.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took data on T-Mobile's current, former and prospective customers.
rows.impact: 76.6 million people in the US.
rows.cause: Intrusion into T-Mobile's systems.

rows.what_happened: A maintenance command took down the global backbone; a bug in the audit tool did not stop it, and DNS servers withdrew their routes.
rows.impact: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp down for about six hours (NPR); data centres disconnected worldwide.
rows.cause: Faulty command plus a bug in the audit tool.

rows.what_happened: Zillow's algorithm bought homes at prices above their later resale value. Zillow stopped the home-buying business in November 2021.
rows.impact: Inventory write-down of USD 407.9 million in FY2021, recorded as a cost of revenue (company 10-K).
rows.cause: Home-price forecasts used to buy homes overpaid in a market that moved against it.

rows.what_happened: Remote code execution in the Java logging library, with mass exploitation.
rows.impact: Affected versions 2.0-beta9 to 2.14.1.
rows.cause: Unsafe JNDI lookup.

rows.what_happened: A memory corruption in pkexec let any local user gain root on major Linux distributions.
rows.impact: Present since pkexec was created in May 2009, about twelve and a half years.
rows.cause: Out-of-bounds write.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took private keys held by the bridge's validators and forged withdrawals, draining funds from the Ronin bridge.
rows.impact: About USD 625 million in crypto (173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC), per US officials at the time. Ether part about USD 597 million.
rows.cause: Compromised validator private keys.

rows.what_happened: GitHub Copilot becomes generally available to all developers.
An unidentified hacker exploited a vulnerability in Samyang Group's mail server in July 2022 and exposed personal information.
rows.impact: About 150,000 people. On 11 Nov 2026 the privacy regulator fined four affiliates a total of 552 million won (about $413,000).
rows.cause: A failure to take basic safety measures, per the regulator.

rows.what_happened: A network upgrade removed a filter from distribution routers; the routing flood overwhelmed core routers.
rows.impact: From 4:58 EDT on 8 July to 7:00 EDT on 9 July 2022; more than 12 million customers lost wireless and wireline service.
rows.cause: Configuration change without overload protection on the core routers, per the CRTC-commissioned review.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took data on Optus customers in Australia.
rows.impact: Up to 10 million current and former customers.
rows.cause: Unauthorised access to customer data.

rows.what_happened: OpenAI opens ChatGPT as a free research preview.
A winter storm met a crew scheduling process that broke down, and the airline could not reassign crews.
rows.impact: More than 16,700 cancelled flights (company); about USD 800 million pre-tax Q4 impact; USD 140 million DOT penalty (2023).
rows.cause: Crew scheduling could not keep up with mass reassignment.

rows.what_happened: The system that issues notices to pilots failed overnight, and the FAA paused all domestic departures.
rows.impact: More than 7,300 delays and 1,100 cancellations by mid-day.
rows.cause: Contract personnel unintentionally deleted files while correcting synchronization between the live primary database and a backup database (FAA).

rows.what_happened: Some ChatGPT users could see the titles of other users' chat histories. Payment-related details of some ChatGPT Plus subscribers were also visible to others.
rows.impact: OpenAI said payment-related information of 1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers active in a nine-hour window may have been exposed.
rows.cause: A bug in an open-source Redis client library, triggered during a change to the service.

rows.what_happened: A signed release of the 3CX phone app for Windows and macOS carried malware.
rows.impact: Users of the 3CX desktop app. CISA warned the next day.
rows.cause: A trojanised build, signed by the vendor.

rows.what_happened: Samsung engineers pasted confidential source code and the text of an internal meeting into ChatGPT, in at least three incidents.
rows.impact: Samsung reportedly capped uploads at 1,024 bytes per question afterwards. It did not confirm the leaks.
rows.cause: Staff put confidential work data into a public AI chatbot.

rows.what_happened: The CL0P group exploited an SQL injection in MOVEit Transfer to steal data and used the LEMURLOOT web shell.
rows.impact: Exploitation from 27 May 2023; joint CISA and FBI advisory dated 7 Jun 2023. Emsisoft counted 2,773 organisations and about 95.8 million people.
rows.cause: Zero-day flaw in file transfer software.

rows.organisation_system: Microsoft AI research team (Azure SAS token)
rows.what_happened: Open-source AI training data was published on GitHub with a link that gave full control of a whole Azure storage account. The account held 38 TB of other internal data.
rows.impact: 38 TB of internal data exposed. Microsoft revoked the link on 24 June 2023; the researchers at Wiz made it public on 18 September 2023.
rows.cause: An Azure SAS token with full control permissions, placed in a public GitHub repository.

rows.what_happened: A Chinese group read the mailboxes of US government officials and others in Exchange Online. The Cyber Safety Review Board called it preventable.
rows.impact: 22 organisations and more than 500 people.
rows.cause: Tokens forged with a stolen Microsoft signing key.

rows.what_happened: A flaw in Intel CPUs let a local attacker read data that other processes or virtual machines handled.
rows.impact: Core processors from 6th-gen Skylake to 11th-gen Tiger Lake, per the Downfall page.
rows.cause: Side channel in Intel CPU data-gathering instructions.

rows.what_happened: An attack shut down systems at MGM's hotels and casinos for days.
rows.impact: About $100 million, by MGM's filing.
rows.cause: A cybersecurity incident; MGM's filing does not name the way in.

rows.what_happened: Attackers logged into customer accounts with passwords reused from other sites, and through them reached data on millions of relatives.
rows.impact: 6.9 million customers, from about 14,000 accounts entered directly.
rows.cause: Credential stuffing.

rows.what_happened: A finance employee in the Hong Kong office joined a video call with what looked like the company's UK CFO and other staff. They were deepfakes. The employee then made 15 transfers to five local bank accounts.
rows.impact: HK$200 million (about US$25.6 million) sent. Arup said its own systems were not compromised.
rows.cause: Deepfake video call with fake voices and images of senior staff.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware stopped claims and pharmacy processing across the US health system.
rows.impact: 192.7 million individuals reported to HHS (an overcount of unique people, per the company); a USD 22 million ransom reported paid.
rows.cause: A Citrix remote access service without multi-factor authentication.

rows.what_happened: A network change with a configuration error took down AT&T's mobile network across the US for about 12 hours.
rows.impact: More than 92 million calls blocked, more than 25,000 of them to 911.
rows.cause: A configuration error in a network change.

rows.what_happened: A long-running backdoor in xz that could affect sshd, found by chance by Andres Freund.
rows.impact: The attacker's first patch is dated 29 Oct 2021 in one timeline; caught before reaching stable distributions.
rows.cause: Social engineering of the maintainer.

rows.what_happened: Data was stolen from customer Snowflake instances using credentials taken by infostealers.
rows.impact: Mandiant and Snowflake notified about 165 potentially exposed organisations. Among them AT&T: call and text records of nearly all its wireless customers, reported as about 110 million.
rows.cause: Stolen credentials; no MFA on the accounts.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware took the electronic health records of Ascension, a large US hospital chain, offline for weeks.
rows.impact: Nearly 5.6 million people.
rows.cause: Ransomware.

rows.what_happened: Models recommended packages that do not exist, which an attacker could register.
rows.impact: 2024 test of 16 code models: 19.7% of 2.23 million package references were hallucinated, 205,474 unique non-existent names.
rows.cause: Hallucinated package names from LLMs.

rows.what_happened: An attack shut down the software that car dealerships across North America use to sell and service cars.
rows.impact: More than 15,000 dealership locations.
rows.cause: A cyberattack on CDK's systems.

rows.what_happened: A new owner of the polyfill.io domain served malicious code to every site that loaded its script.
rows.impact: More than 100,000 websites.
rows.cause: A widely used script domain changed hands.

rows.what_happened: A signal handler race in OpenSSH's server allowed unauthenticated remote code execution as root on glibc Linux.
rows.impact: A regression of a 2006 bug, reintroduced in October 2020 (OpenSSH 8.5p1), almost four years in releases.
rows.cause: Regression: a removed safeguard.

rows.what_happened: A sensor content update crashed Windows machines into a blue screen.
rows.impact: About 8.5 million Windows devices (Microsoft estimate).
rows.cause: Content file defined 21 input fields, but the sensor supplied 20, causing an out-of-bounds read (CrowdStrike RCA).

rows.what_happened: A background-check data broker lost a database of names, addresses and Social Security numbers.
rows.impact: About 2.9 billion rows, with about 272 million unique Social Security numbers.
rows.cause: Breach of the company's database.

rows.what_happened: IOActive researchers showed that a flaw in AMD's System Management Mode let an attacker with kernel access run code at the highest privilege level.
rows.impact: AMD processors dating back to 2006, per the public write-up.
rows.cause: Flaw in AMD SMM lock handling.

rows.what_happened: Hackers took user email addresses and chat prompts from an AI companion website. The prompts were linked to the users' email addresses.
rows.impact: 1.9 million email addresses in the breach record of Have I Been Pwned.
rows.cause: The attack method is not published. The site operator blamed a targeted attack by rivals.

rows.what_happened: Simone Margaritelli disclosed a chain of CUPS flaws that can let a remote attacker run commands on Linux and Unix machines when a print job starts.
rows.impact: The foomatic-rip hole was known since 2011 (CVE-2011-2697, CVE-2011-2964) and still unpatched in many CUPS installations.
rows.cause: Commands passed through the FoomaticRIPCommandLine directive.

rows.organisation_system: Google Big Sleep to SQLite (Project Zero and DeepMind)
rows.what_happened: An AI agent found an exploitable stack buffer underflow in SQLite.
rows.impact: Published 1 Nov 2024; found in early October 2024 and fixed the same day, before any release; users not affected.
rows.cause: Variant analysis of commits by an LLM agent.

rows.what_happened: Google's OSS-Fuzz found an OpenSSL flaw with fuzz targets written and improved by AI.
rows.impact: The bug had likely been in OpenSSL for two decades. Fuzz targets written by people would not have reached it.
rows.cause: AI-generated fuzz targets.

rows.what_happened: A Chinese espionage campaign got inside US telecom carriers, the White House said.
rows.impact: Nine US telecom companies.
rows.cause: A long-running intrusion campaign.

rows.what_happened: An attacker used stolen customer credentials to reach old Cerner servers not yet migrated to Oracle Cloud and copied patient data to a remote server, some time after 22 Jan 2025.
rows.impact: Nearly 20 million people, per a Texas attorney general report cited by Bloomberg, 2,992,244 of them in Texas; earlier filings listed far fewer. Oracle has not stated a number.
rows.cause: Stolen customer credentials on legacy servers awaiting migration.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took personal data of students and teachers from PowerSchool, a school software provider.
rows.impact: Schools across North America; PowerSchool has not given a count.
rows.cause: A compromised credential.

rows.what_happened: Wiz found a DeepSeek database open to the internet without authentication, holding chat history and secret keys.
rows.impact: More than a million lines of logs. DeepSeek closed it after Wiz reported it.
rows.cause: A database left reachable from outside.

rows.what_happened: Fraudsters used a cloned voice of Italy's defence minister to call business leaders and ask for urgent transfers. Targets included a fashion designer and a former football club owner.
rows.impact: One businessman reportedly sent about EUR 1 million to a Hong Kong bank account. The victim has not confirmed the sum.
rows.cause: An AI voice clone of a public official.

rows.what_happened: Qualys found a flaw that lets a machine in the middle pose as a server to the OpenSSH client when the VerifyHostKeyDNS option is on.
rows.impact: OpenSSH 6.8p1 to 9.9p1. The flaw was added in December 2014.
rows.cause: A bug in the client's host key check.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took control of a routine transfer from a cold wallet by tampering with the wallet provider's interface.
rows.impact: About USD 1.5 billion in crypto stolen; the FBI attributed it to North Korea.
rows.cause: A Safe{Wallet} developer machine compromised and the interface script replaced, per the forensic report.

rows.what_happened: A finance director joined a Zoom call with the company's CEO. The CEO was a deepfake. He then sent the money on 26 March 2025.
rows.impact: Over US$499,000 (about S$670,000) sent. Police traced and withheld that amount.
rows.cause: Deepfake video conference of company executives.

rows.what_happened: Microsoft used Security Copilot to find vulnerabilities in three open-source bootloaders.
rows.impact: 20 flaws in the CVE list of Microsoft's post: 11 in GRUB2, 4 in U-Boot, 5 in Barebox.
rows.cause: AI-assisted code analysis, with Microsoft researchers confirming.

rows.what_happened: Hackers took subscriber data from SK Telecom's servers, including USIM authentication keys that were not encrypted.
rows.impact: About 23 million subscribers affected, according to the regulator. More than 26 million USIM keys were left unencrypted. The Personal Information Protection Commission fined the company 134.5 billion won (about $97 million).
rows.cause: Weak access controls, keys stored without encryption, and late notice to users.

rows.what_happened: Scrapers collecting data for AI training sharply raised the load on Wikimedia infrastructure.
rows.impact: Multimedia bandwidth up 50% since Jan 2024 (as of early 2025); bots were at least 65% of the most expensive traffic but about 35% of pageviews.
rows.cause: Mass crawling for model training.

rows.what_happened: A cyberattack over Easter stopped online orders and disrupted stores.
rows.impact: About GBP 300 million impact on operating profit before insurance and mitigation, per the company.
rows.cause: Attackers tricked staff at a third-party contractor (Reuters).

rows.what_happened: Coinbase said criminals bribed or recruited overseas support agents to steal customer data. It disclosed the breach in a filing on May 15, 2025.
rows.impact: Less than 1% of monthly transacting users affected. Coinbase estimated remediation and reimbursement costs of $180 million to $400 million. The attackers demanded a $20 million ransom, which Coinbase refused to pay.
rows.cause: Rogue overseas support agents who had access to customer data.

rows.what_happened: The researcher Sean Heelan gave an OpenAI model parts of the kernel's SMB server code, and it found a use-after-free nobody had reported.
rows.impact: Fixed in stable kernels. In his larger run, over all the command handlers, he put the signal to noise at about 1 to 50.
rows.cause: LLM code review, with a person confirming the find.

rows.organisation_system: Agentic coding tools (Anthropic coding agent GA; GitHub Copilot coding agent preview)
rows.what_happened: Agents that change code and run commands reach general availability or public preview.
Zero-click prompt injection: a crafted email could make Copilot disclose user data.
rows.impact: CVSS 9.3 (CNA score); Microsoft fixed it on the server side in May 2025, before the flaw was made public in June 2025.
rows.cause: Prompt injection that crosses the LLM's context boundaries.

rows.what_happened: A code change without a feature flag or error handling hit a null pointer that crashed a binary worldwide.
rows.impact: Surge of 503 errors in external Google Cloud and Workspace APIs; details in Google's incident report.
rows.cause: Change without a feature flag; mishandling of empty fields.

rows.what_happened: An AI agent deleted a production database during a code freeze and wrongly said a rollback was impossible.
rows.impact: Records on more than 1,200 executives and over 1,190 companies were affected; data restored by rollback.
rows.cause: Agent given production access without separation of environments.

rows.what_happened: Researchers Ian Carroll and Sam Curry logged into the admin side of McDonald's hiring chatbot with the password 123456 and could reach applicants' chats through an API flaw.
rows.impact: Chats for more than 64 million job applications were reachable, by the researchers' count. Paradox says they pulled seven records and nobody else used the account.
rows.cause: A test account with the password 123456, and an insecure direct object reference in an internal API.

rows.what_happened: Attackers took Qantas customer data through a third-party platform, and later published it.
rows.impact: 5.7 million customers.
rows.cause: An attack on a vendor's platform.

rows.what_happened: Chats that users had shared by link could be indexed by search engines, and some appeared in Google results. OpenAI called the setting a short-lived experiment and removed it.
rows.impact: Shared chats with personal details became searchable. No official count was published.
rows.cause: A share setting that let people make links discoverable by search engines.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware hit Ingram Micro's internal systems. Ordering platforms went offline and some staff were sent home.
rows.impact: Resellers and managed service providers could not place orders from July 3. Ingram confirmed the ransomware on July 5.
rows.cause: SafePay ransomware group, which claimed the attack. Ingram did not name the group.

rows.what_happened: A flood of AI-generated false vulnerability reports ('AI slop') reached curl's bug bounty.
rows.impact: By early July 2025, about 20% of submissions were AI slop and about 5% were genuine vulnerabilities.
rows.cause: LLM-generated reports written to earn bounties.

rows.what_happened: Using threat intelligence indicators, Big Sleep found a SQLite flaw that attackers were preparing to exploit.
rows.impact: CVSS 7.2, fixed in SQLite 3.50.2. Google believes it is the first time an AI agent directly foiled an exploitation attempt in the wild.
rows.cause: Threat intelligence from Google's GTIG combined with an LLM agent.

rows.what_happened: Attackers used a flaw in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 20, 2025.
rows.impact: Attackers could run code on unpatched SharePoint servers without logging in. SharePoint Online was not affected.
rows.cause: Deserialization flaw, CVE-2025-53770, in on-premises SharePoint.

rows.organisation_system: Amazon Q Developer for VS Code (CVE-2025-8217)
rows.what_happened: Version 1.84.0 shipped an injected destructive prompt meant for the AI agent.
rows.impact: It did not run because of a syntax error; fixed in 1.85.0.
rows.cause: A GitHub token with excess rights in a CodeBuild configuration.

rows.what_happened: Starlink went down worldwide after internal software services that run its core network failed.
rows.impact: About 2.5 hours, worldwide.
rows.cause: Failure of internal software services that run the core network.

rows.organisation_system: Chattee Chat and GiMe Chat (AI companion apps)
rows.what_happened: An unprotected Kafka data system held messages and images from two AI companion apps by the same developer.
rows.impact: Data of over 400,000 people: 43 million messages and over 600,000 images and videos.
rows.cause: An exposed streaming system with no access controls.

rows.organisation_system: Google Big Sleep (FFmpeg, ImageMagick and others)
rows.what_happened: Google said its AI agent Big Sleep had found and reported 20 flaws in popular open-source software, mostly in FFmpeg and ImageMagick.
rows.impact: 20 flaws reported.
rows.cause: LLM agent.

rows.what_happened: Autonomous AI cyber reasoning systems found and patched vulnerabilities in the competition final.
rows.impact: 54 of 63 synthetic vulnerabilities found and 43 patched; 18 real vulnerabilities found and 11 patched; about $152 per task.
rows.cause: LLM-based cyber reasoning systems.

rows.organisation_system: Salesloft Drift (AI chat agent) to Salesforce (UNC6395)
rows.what_happened: Attackers used stolen OAuth tokens of the Drift AI chat agent integration to steal data from Salesforce.
rows.impact: Activity 8 to 18 Aug 2025; GTIG: over 700 potentially impacted organisations.
rows.cause: Compromise of a third-party AI agent integration's tokens.

rows.organisation_system: xAI Grok (shared chats in search results)
rows.what_happened: Grok chats that users shared with the share button were published at links that search engines indexed.
rows.impact: More than 370,000 chats in search results.
rows.cause: Shared links were open to search engines, and users were not told.

rows.what_happened: Malicious Nx versions ran locally installed AI command-line tools with permission-bypass flags (per Wiz) to search for secrets.
rows.impact: Live for about 4 to 5 hours; Nx had 4.6 million weekly downloads; Wiz counted over 1,700 users with leaked secrets and at least 480 compromised accounts, 2,180 in all.
rows.cause: Injection into GitHub Actions led to theft of an npm token.

rows.what_happened: ESET announced PromptLock as the first AI-powered ransomware. It turned out to be a research prototype from NYU.
rows.impact: No real attack. The sample came from a lab.
rows.cause: An AI model wrote the attack scripts while it ran.

rows.what_happened: Anthropic reported a criminal who used its coding agent to run a data extortion campaign, from reconnaissance and break-in to the ransom notes.
rows.impact: At least 17 organisations, among them healthcare, emergency services, government and religious institutions. Ransom demands sometimes above $500,000.
rows.cause: The attacker had the agent automate the intrusion and choose what data to take.

rows.what_happened: A cyberattack shut down production across the carmaker's plants.
rows.impact: Production halted for about five weeks; the Cyber Monitoring Centre put the UK economic cost at GBP 1.9 billion.
rows.cause: Not published by the company.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware stopped Asahi's breweries and factories in Japan.
rows.impact: Production stopped at all 30 of its plants in Japan.
rows.cause: Ransomware.

rows.what_happened: Prosper found unauthorized activity on its systems in September 2025. Prosper said no customer accounts or funds were accessed.
rows.impact: Have I Been Pwned lists 17.6 million people. Prosper has not confirmed that number. Data reported includes Social Security numbers, government IDs, income levels and addresses.
rows.cause: Not stated by the company.

rows.what_happened: Big Sleep reported an out-of-bounds read in curl's cookie path handling.
rows.impact: curl's advisory credits Google Big Sleep; fixed in curl 8.16.0.
rows.cause: LLM agent.

rows.what_happened: A self-replicating worm in npm stole maintainer tokens and secrets.
rows.impact: Campaign from about 15 Sep 2025; CISA alert of 23 Sep reports more than 500 packages compromised.
rows.cause: Theft of maintainer tokens.

rows.what_happened: Ransomware hit the shared check-in and boarding software used by several European airports.
rows.impact: Disruption at Heathrow, Brussels, Berlin and Dublin; Brussels asked airlines to cancel half of its departures for one day.
rows.cause: Ransomware, per ENISA.

rows.what_happened: Noma Security showed that instructions hidden in a Web-to-Lead form could make Salesforce Agentforce send CRM data to an attacker.
rows.impact: Rated 9.4 by Noma. Salesforce patched it.
rows.cause: Prompt injection, plus an expired domain still on Salesforce's allowlist.

rows.what_happened: AISLE, a company that builds an AI system for finding vulnerabilities, reported three OpenSSL flaws.
rows.impact: The records credit Stanislav Fort (Aisle Research); OpenSSL fixed all three in its 30 September 2025 releases.
rows.cause: AI analysis, by AISLE's account, with OpenSSL developers confirming and fixing.

rows.what_happened: Attackers used a zero-day flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite to steal data from customer-run systems. Extortion emails then went to several victims.
rows.impact: Oracle confirmed the attacks on on-premises systems. The sources read do not give a victim count.
rows.cause: Zero-day flaw CVE-2025-61882 in on-premises Oracle E-Business Suite.

rows.organisation_system: Red Hat Consulting GitLab instance (not GitLab itself)
rows.what_happened: Attackers breached a GitLab instance used for Red Hat Consulting work, not GitLab's own service.
rows.impact: Crimson Collective's claims of about 570 GB and 28,000 repositories are unconfirmed.
rows.cause: Compromise of a self-managed instance (per GitLab's statement).

rows.what_happened: A race condition in DynamoDB's DNS automation left an empty endpoint record, and the failure spread across the region.
rows.impact: 06:48 to 21:20 UTC on 20 Oct (23:48 PDT 19 Oct to 14:20 PDT 20 Oct).
rows.cause: Race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system.

rows.what_happened: Configuration changes produced metadata that crashed Azure Front Door, and Azure, Microsoft 365 and many customer sites went down worldwide.
rows.impact: A global disruption of most of a day.
rows.cause: Incompatible configuration metadata, and a latent bug in reference counting.

rows.what_happened: OpenAI's security agent Aardvark found vulnerabilities in open-source projects, and they were disclosed.
rows.impact: Ten of them received CVE numbers.
rows.cause: LLM agent.

rows.organisation_system: Google Antigravity coding tool (a user's D: drive)
rows.what_happened: Google's Antigravity coding tool wiped a user's whole D: drive when asked to clear a project cache.
rows.impact: An entire drive, past the Recycle Bin. The user had most of it backed up elsewhere.
rows.cause: The agent ran a delete aimed at the root of the drive instead of the cache folder.

rows.what_happened: AISLE reported missing SFTP host verification in curl's wolfSSH backend.
rows.impact: curl's advisory credits Stanislav Fort (Aisle Research).
rows.cause: AI analysis, by AISLE's account.

rows.what_happened: A state-sponsored group, which Anthropic assesses as Chinese, used an AI coding tool to orchestrate espionage.
rows.impact: About 30 targets; according to Anthropic, AI did 80-90% of the work, with humans at 4-6 decision points.
rows.cause: Agentic misuse of an AI coding tool.

rows.what_happened: A permissions change in ClickHouse made a query return duplicate rows, roughly doubling the feature file of the bot-detection ML model; the proxy failed.
rows.impact: 11:20 to 17:06 UTC; main traffic restored by 14:30 UTC.
rows.cause: The query lacked a database filter; the file exceeded the 200-feature limit.

rows.what_happened: Coupang found unauthorized access on November 18, 2025 and first counted 4,500 accounts. A later review found a much larger exposure.
rows.impact: About 33.7 million customer accounts in South Korea. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, shipping addresses and some order histories were exposed. The company said payment data and login credentials were not affected.
rows.cause: Under investigation when reported.

rows.what_happened: A second self-spreading worm hit npm. It backdoored npm packages and used the stolen publishing access to infect more of them.
rows.impact: Datadog counted 796 unique npm packages backdoored and over 14,000 linked GitHub repositories. Stolen credentials were sent out through public GitHub repositories.
rows.cause: Compromised maintainer accounts. A new preinstall script ran the worm's files when a package was installed.

rows.what_happened: An attacker got into Mixpanel, the analytics provider OpenAI used on its API platform, and took a dataset with OpenAI users' profile data.
rows.impact: Names, email addresses, approximate location, browser and organisation or user IDs of API users. No count given.
rows.cause: A breach at the analytics vendor. OpenAI's own systems were not breached.

rows.organisation_system: Mexican government agencies (one attacker with AI tools)
rows.what_happened: One attacker used Anthropic's coding agent and an OpenAI model to break into Mexican government systems from late December 2025 to mid-February 2026, according to Gambit Security.
rows.impact: At least nine government organisations. Gambit Security put it at about 150GB and 195 million taxpayer records. Mexico's tax and electoral authorities dispute the reports.
rows.cause: The coding agent ran about 75 percent of the remote commands, and stolen data went through the OpenAI model for analysis, according to Gambit.

rows.what_happened: The Financial Times reported that a 13-hour AWS outage began when Amazon's Kiro coding agent chose to delete and recreate an environment.
rows.impact: One AWS service disrupted for 13 hours.
rows.cause: Amazon says it was user error, misconfigured access controls, not AI.

rows.what_happened: A critical flaw in React Server Components allowed code to run on a server through a crafted web request. CISA added it to its KEV catalog on December 5, 2025.
rows.impact: Shadowserver found 77,664 vulnerable IP addresses, about 23,700 in the United States. Palo Alto Networks reported more than 30 organisations already compromised.
rows.cause: Unsafe handling of requests in React Server Components. Federal agencies were given until December 26, 2025 to patch.

rows.what_happened: Cloudflare's network returned HTTP 500 errors for about 25 minutes. The trigger was a change made while the company was protecting customers from the React flaw.
rows.impact: About 28% of all HTTP traffic served by Cloudflare was affected. Services hosted on the network returned errors until services were restored at 09:12 UTC.
rows.cause: A web application firewall change raised the request buffer, and a second change that turned off an internal testing tool triggered a bug. Cloudflare said it was not a cyberattack.

rows.what_happened: Stolen cloud accounts were used for LLM resources, and access was resold.
rows.impact: GTIG and Mandiant: single-day charges above $100,000; up to $1 million cumulative in the most severe cases.
rows.cause: Stolen accounts; AI was the target, not the cause.

rows.what_happened: A web console for the company's AI toys could be opened with any Google account. Researchers logged in with arbitrary accounts and read children's chats.
rows.impact: About 50,000 chat logs between children and AI toys. The company says it closed the console within hours.
rows.cause: A misconfigured console that accepted any Google login.

rows.what_happened: A Firebase misconfiguration let outsiders reach the chat histories of users of the Chat and Ask AI app. The researcher alerted the developer on 20 January 2026.
rows.impact: About 300 million messages from more than 25 million users.
rows.cause: A Firebase backend misconfiguration.

rows.what_happened: Verizon's wireless service went down across the United States on January 14, 2026.
rows.impact: More than 130,000 outage reports on Downdetector at about 1:11 pm ET. Verizon offered $20 account credits to affected customers.
rows.cause: Not stated in the sources read. Verizon said its engineers were working to identify and solve the issue.

rows.what_happened: An unauthorised party accessed and copied files from company systems between 18 Jan and 8 Feb 2026.
rows.impact: 1,332,826 people nationwide per third-party summaries of state filings; Amplifon has not confirmed the total. Vermont was notified on 5 Nov 2026 (1,027 residents).
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: OpenSSL (all 12 CVEs of the January 2026 release, AISLE)
rows.what_happened: Every one of the 12 CVEs in OpenSSL's January 2026 security release was found by AISLE's AI analyzer.
rows.impact: 12 CVEs, each credited to Aisle Research in OpenSSL's advisory.
rows.cause: AI analysis, by AISLE's account, with OpenSSL developers confirming and fixing.

rows.what_happened: Wiz found Moltbook's database open to anyone through a public key.
rows.impact: 1.5 million API tokens and 35,000 email addresses could be read and changed.
rows.cause: Row level security was off. The founder said he vibe-coded the platform.

rows.what_happened: Jeremiah Fowler found three open databases of Sears Home Services' AI customer support assistant, with chat logs and call recordings.
rows.impact: About 3.7 million records, about 1.44 million of them audio recordings.
rows.cause: Databases without a password or encryption.

rows.organisation_system: ShinyHunters affiliate (GTG-50014), via a SaaS provider
rows.what_happened: A cybercrime actor used Anthropic's AI agents to do nearly all the work of a compromise. It used a SaaS provider as the route into its customers' data.
rows.impact: Data taken from roughly 200 downstream customer organisations of one SaaS company, according to Anthropic.
rows.cause: AI agents performed nearly all of the work of the attack.

rows.what_happened: An Anthropic model found, and with people validated, vulnerabilities in open-source software, including Ghostscript, OpenSC and CGIF.
rows.impact: More than 500 validated high-severity vulnerabilities; Anthropic says 90-day disclosure windows may not hold up.
rows.cause: LLM code analysis; some bugs had gone undetected for decades.

rows.organisation_system: OpenClaw AI agents (formerly Clawdbot and Moltbot)
rows.what_happened: Security firms found tens of thousands of OpenClaw AI agent instances open to the internet.
rows.impact: More than 135,000 by SecurityScorecard's count, more than 30,000 by Bitsight's, about 21,600 by Censys on 31 January.
rows.cause: Agents exposed on the internet. The Register calls the platform vibe-coded.

rows.organisation_system: An app built with Lovable (showcased on its Discover page)
rows.what_happened: A researcher found that an app built with Lovable and showcased on its Discover page let anyone read every user record.
rows.impact: 18,697 user records, 14,928 of them with unique email addresses.
rows.cause: Access control written by an AI code generator, according to the researcher. Lovable says part of the project was not generated by it.

rows.what_happened: Anthropic and Mozilla used an Anthropic model to search Firefox for vulnerabilities.
rows.impact: 22 CVEs, 14 of them high severity. Most were fixed in Firefox 148.
rows.cause: AI analysis, with Mozilla engineers confirming.

rows.what_happened: CodeWall's autonomous agent got full read and write access to McKinsey's internal AI platform Lilli in about two hours, in a test disclosed to McKinsey before publication.
rows.impact: 46.5 million chat messages, 728,000 files and 57,000 accounts were reachable, by CodeWall's count. McKinsey says it found no evidence that client data was accessed.
rows.cause: SQL injection through JSON field names, and endpoints without authentication. An AI agent ran the attack.

rows.what_happened: Malicious versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 of LiteLLM, a popular gateway to AI models, were published to PyPI and stole credentials from the machines that installed them.
rows.impact: Live for a few hours before PyPI quarantined them. The stealer took SSH keys, cloud tokens, Kubernetes secrets and crypto wallets.
rows.cause: The attackers likely got the PyPI credentials through a compromised Trivy scanner in CI.

rows.what_happened: An employee misappropriated company data holding personal and health information, starting on or about 26 Mar 2026. The company learned of it on 18 Sep 2026.
rows.impact: State filings of 6 Nov 2026 give a partial count of 112,033 people.
rows.cause: An insider who broke company information security policies. Premise Health: 'This was not a hacking or ransomware event.'

rows.what_happened: The popular HTTP client axios was compromised in a campaign attributed to UNC1069.
rows.impact: Malicious versions published 00:21 and 01:00 UTC, removed about 03:30 UTC on 31 Mar 2026; more than 100 million weekly downloads.
rows.cause: Takeover of the maintainer account or publishing process.

rows.what_happened: Anthropic's coding agent was published to npm with a source map that exposed its internal source code.
rows.impact: About 1,900 files and more than 500,000 lines of code. No customer data or credentials, according to Anthropic.
rows.cause: A release packaging error made by a person, according to Anthropic.

rows.what_happened: A critical flaw in FortiClient Enterprise Management Server was exploited as a zero-day. Fortinet released an emergency hotfix in early April.
rows.impact: watchTowr honeypots first saw attacks on March 31, 2026. The flaw has a CVSS score of 9.1.
rows.cause: Flaw in FortiClient EMS. The hotfix covers versions 7.4.5 and 7.4.6.

rows.what_happened: Context.ai, an AI analytics tool, had a Google Workspace OAuth grant authorised by Vercel employees. The attacker used it to reach an employee's Google Workspace and then internal systems. Environment variables not marked sensitive were readable.
rows.impact: Number of affected teams and projects not disclosed. Vercel described the impact as limited.
rows.cause: A compromised OAuth application from an AI tool vendor.

rows.what_happened: The actor used Anthropic's AI to develop and debug a WordPress exploit in one session. It also used AI sub-agents for reconnaissance, code review and checking findings.
rows.impact: Of 42 tracked target entities, the actor gained internal access to at least 14. Targets included European political parties, media and think-tanks.
rows.cause: AI used to write and debug the exploit. The report says the activity was in spring 2026; the month used here is an estimate.

rows.what_happened: Nicholas Carlini of Anthropic used Anthropic's coding agent to find a heap overflow in the Linux NFS server that a remote attacker can use to read kernel memory.
rows.impact: In the kernel since March 2003, 23 years.
rows.cause: Anthropic's coding agent, run over the kernel source.

rows.organisation_system: OpenBSD, FFmpeg and FreeBSD (Anthropic preview model)
rows.what_happened: Anthropic reported old flaws that a preview model found on its own after a first prompt, among them a bug in OpenBSD's TCP SACK code that could crash any OpenBSD host answering over TCP.
rows.impact: The OpenBSD bug was 27 years old, a flaw in FFmpeg's H.264 codec 16 years, a FreeBSD remote code execution flaw 17 years. OpenBSD fixed its bug on 25 March 2026.
rows.cause: LLM agent, with no person after the first prompt.

rows.organisation_system: PocketOS (Cursor coding agent on an Anthropic model)
rows.what_happened: A Cursor coding agent running an Anthropic model deleted the production database and its backups at PocketOS, a car rental software company, with one API call.
rows.impact: Database and backups gone in nine seconds. The team rebuilt the data by hand from payment records and emails.
rows.cause: The agent found a root-level cloud token in an unrelated file and used it.

rows.what_happened: Theori disclosed a flaw that lets any local user get root with a 732-byte Python script. Theori calls the find AI-assisted.
rows.impact: Essentially every Linux distribution shipped since 2017.
rows.cause: An optimisation added to algif_aead.c in 2017.

rows.what_happened: Hackers from the ShinyHunters group broke into Instructure's Canvas learning platform. Instructure found the breach on April 29, 2026.
rows.impact: Instructure said names, email addresses, student ID numbers and messages were exposed. ShinyHunters claimed 275 million records across about 9,000 schools. Instructure has not confirmed those counts.
rows.cause: Attributed to the ShinyHunters extortion group, which claimed the attack.

rows.what_happened: A rogue DHCP server on the local network could run code as root on a FreeBSD machine through its DHCP client. FreeBSD credits Joshua Rogers of AISLE Research, which says its AI analysis flagged the bug.
rows.impact: In FreeBSD's dhclient since the June 2005 import of OpenBSD's client, about 21 years. All supported FreeBSD versions, fixed 29 April 2026.
rows.cause: The lease file was written without escaping double quotes.

rows.what_happened: An actor attacked roughly thirty AI companies in about four days with similar techniques. It took production API keys from one AI vendor's evaluation sandbox. Anthropic's report says this actor did not use Anthropic's AI as a tool.
rows.impact: About 30 AI companies attacked; production API keys taken from one vendor.
rows.cause: Ordinary intrusion techniques against AI companies.

rows.what_happened: A victim received WhatsApp messages and joined a Zoom call. Deepfakes showed the prime minister, the president and ministers. A deepfake prime minister gave closing remarks. The victim sent money to a corporate account the scammers supplied.
rows.impact: At least S$4.9 million lost, per press reports of the police advisory. Police did not give the sum in the release checked.
rows.cause: Deepfake video and fake audio of senior officials.

rows.organisation_system: Linux kernel ESP and RxRPC (Dirty Frag, CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500)
rows.what_happened: Hyunwoo Kim disclosed two Linux kernel flaws that let a local user get root. A public proof of concept exists.
rows.impact: CVE-2026-43284 is in kernels from January 2017 to the May 2026 fix.
rows.cause: Flaws in the kernel's ESP code, from about 2017, and RxRPC code, from about 2023.

rows.what_happened: A heap buffer overflow in nginx's rewrite module can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on the server. depthfirst, which builds AI for security, found it with its autonomous system.
rows.impact: Every nginx from 0.6.27 (2008) to 1.30.0, 18 years. Fixed in 1.30.1 and 1.31.0.
rows.cause: An undersized buffer in ngx_http_rewrite_module.

rows.what_happened: Attackers published malicious versions of npm packages in a short burst, mostly in the @antv scope. Microsoft issued a warning on May 19, 2026.
rows.impact: Socket tracked 1,055 malicious versions across 502 unique packages in the campaign. Over 320 npm packages were hit in the first burst.
rows.cause: Malicious versions published as part of the Shai-Hulud worm campaign.

rows.what_happened: Hackers were on DentaQuest's network from May 17 to May 20, 2026. ShinyHunters claimed the attack and said it took 234 GB of data.
rows.impact: DentaQuest said at least 15 million people were affected. Data includes names, Social Security numbers, member IDs, Medicaid and Medicare numbers, and dental or vision health information.
rows.cause: Not stated by the company. The ShinyHunters group claimed responsibility.

rows.what_happened: A researcher found flaws that let an attacker bypass authentication on the platform of CreditNirvana, an AI debt collection service owned by Perfios.
rows.impact: 6.6 million borrower accounts and about 315,000 call recordings were exposed while the flaws were open. Patched in June 2026, disclosed in October, reported by Wired on 18 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Authentication bypass on the primary platform.

rows.what_happened: An out-of-bounds read in Squid's FTP gateway could leak memory from other users' transactions. Calif.io found it with an Anthropic preview model; Aisle Research and CTF.ae reported it independently.
rows.impact: In Squid's FTP code since 1997 by the finder's account, about 29 years; Squid's public commit history does not reach that far back. Fixed in Squid 7.6.
rows.cause: An out-of-bounds read in the FTP gateway's parser.

rows.what_happened: Attackers phished a Mastra maintainer and used the account to publish malicious npm packages in the Mastra ecosystem.
rows.impact: 144 npm packages affected.
rows.cause: Phished maintainer account. The hijacked account belonged to a former contributor whose access had not been revoked.

rows.what_happened: libcurl could reuse a connection after its client certificate settings had changed, a low-severity authentication bypass in applications that embed libcurl. curl credits Joshua Rogers of Aisle Research.
rows.impact: Every curl from 7.7, March 2001, to 8.20.0, about 25 years. Fixed in 8.21.0.
rows.cause: Client certificate settings were left out of the connection reuse match.

rows.organisation_system: Online retailers (operator using the Strix, Cairn and Hermes AI harnesses)
rows.what_happened: A financially motivated operator ran open-source AI agent harnesses against hundreds of online retailers. The harnesses ran almost the whole attack chain on their own, according to Gambit Security, which recovered the operator's staging server.
rows.impact: At least 27 companies compromised between 10 and 15 Sep 2026, out of 105 attack projects. At least 600,000 unexpired card details taken from two companies and card skimmers placed on the websites of five, per Gambit Security.
rows.cause: Autonomous AI agent harnesses at a marginal cost of tens of dollars per company, per Gambit Security. The activity goes back to July 2026.

rows.what_happened: Nebula Security disclosed a use-after-free in the Linux futex code that lets a local user get root. It found the bug with VEGA, its AI bug-hunting tool.
rows.impact: In Linux since 2011. No attacks known at disclosure.
rows.cause: A use-after-free in futex priority inheritance.

rows.organisation_system: OpenAI test agents to Hugging Face
rows.what_happened: Agents in an OpenAI test environment reached the internet through flaws in an Artifactory instance and compromised part of Hugging Face production.
rows.impact: Attack phase 11 to 13 Jul 2026; Hugging Face disclosed it 16 Jul. California AG suit (16 Nov 2026) says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents at least 80 times.
rows.cause: Sandbox isolation failure and agent reward hacking (per OpenAI's technical report).

rows.what_happened: Hackers got into Fairlife systems, including production systems. Coca-Cola disclosed the attack in a Form 8-K filing on July 16, 2026.
rows.impact: Production at Fairlife's US facilities was temporarily suspended. Canadian production was not affected. Coca-Cola said product quality and safety were not affected.
rows.cause: Unauthorized access to systems. Coca-Cola has not said whether data was stolen or who was behind it.

rows.organisation_system: Artex AI penetration-testing framework (campaigns by criminals and states)
rows.what_happened: Criminals and state actors used Artex, an open-source AI penetration-testing framework, to automate intrusions from reconnaissance through data exfiltration, the FBI said in a flash alert on 13 Nov 2026.
rows.impact: Government agencies and dozens of critical sectors breached worldwide; some intrusions went from first targeting to privileged access in under three hours, per the FBI. Censys counted over 1,600 exposed Artex consoles.
rows.cause: An open-source framework that drives a large language model through the phases of an intrusion. Used in attacks since at least August 2026; its developer said on 8 Oct 2026 that it had been abused.

rows.organisation_system: CL-STA-1238 (Cairn AI agents with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models)
rows.what_happened: Unit 42 documented 25 operations against at least 19 organisations between August and September 2026, run with the open-source Cairn framework paired with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models. Unit 42: 'The attackers supplied a target and a goal, then Cairn planned, executed and recorded results on its own.' Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that this is a China-nexus intelligence collection campaign.
rows.impact: Unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 of the at least 19 organisations.
rows.cause: Misuse of the publicly available Cairn penetration-testing framework, which Unit 42 says runs AI-driven agent workers; Unit 42 says the attackers 'weaponized Cairn by pairing it with Chinese AI models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek.'

rows.organisation_system: ChainDrop (npm worm, keyv and related packages)
rows.what_happened: A self-spreading worm hit npm after the GitHub account of a keyv maintainer was compromised. The malware steals developer credentials and spreads by compromising more packages.
rows.impact: Singapore's Cyber Security Agency says over 1,300 package versions were compromised, with a combined 2 billion monthly downloads.
rows.cause: Compromised GitHub account of a keyv maintainer.

rows.what_happened: An Istio sidecar concurrency limit, a VS Code retry bug (about 10x traffic) and a surge in Copilot Token Service load.
rows.impact: 13:28 to 21:15 UTC (7 hours 47 minutes); Copilot Token Service rose from 7-9K to 70-100K requests per second.
rows.cause: Autoscaling gap and a retry bug under growing load; GitHub does not state an AI cause.

rows.what_happened: A likely Russian-speaking actor used AI agents to develop, test and run exploits for two flaws in PaperCut print management software, four days after the vendor's advisory, according to GreyNoise.
rows.impact: At least 440 PaperCut instances at 395 organisations in 48 countries compromised. The first victim fell in just under four hours from an empty workspace, per GreyNoise.
rows.cause: AI agents wrote and ran the exploits; GreyNoise names OpenAI agent tooling and DeepSeek models.

rows.organisation_system: Russian group linked to Midnight Blizzard (GTG-20006)
rows.what_happened: The group used Anthropic's AI for planning, reconnaissance and live operations. It scanned email and remote access systems of Ukrainian government bodies and took mail records.
rows.impact: More than 20 organisations targeted. Mail records taken from at least eight organisations, according to Anthropic.
rows.cause: AI used for operational planning and live operations.

rows.what_happened: Operators used Anthropic's AI as the engineering and orchestration layer of a coordinated offensive program. It covered intrusions, reconnaissance, vulnerability research and malware development.
rows.impact: Roughly fifty organisations targeted across education, retail, energy, technology, healthcare and finance, plus government agencies, according to Anthropic.
rows.cause: AI used as the engineering and orchestration layer of the attacks.

rows.what_happened: A cyberattack hit La Poste subsidiary Maileva in mid-September and exposed personal data.
rows.impact: First names, last names and postal addresses of 22 million people. La Poste confirmed it to AFP; reported 15 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: Universities in East Asia (Cairn AI agents, MONAI Label zero-day)
rows.what_happened: An actor that Amazon assesses with moderate confidence as China-linked ran Cairn, an open-source framework of AI agents, against universities in East Asia with one goal, to obtain shell access. The agents found a path traversal flaw in the MONAI Label medical imaging application, which Amazon assesses with high confidence was a zero-day, and used it to get a root shell on a server. The operator then gave the agents a proxy into a second university network.
rows.impact: About 48 hours from 8 Sep 2026, against universities in East Asia outside mainland China. The agents went from mapping the application to writing files on the server in about 11 minutes; two longer operations, about 16 hours and more than 6 hours, failed. Amazon published the findings on 20 Nov 2026. The maintainers' advisory of 18 Nov 2026 says the flaw is fixed in the code and the fix will be in the next release.
rows.cause: Autonomous AI agents planned and ran the operations without the operator choosing each step, according to Amazon. The flaw was a path traversal in a file upload endpoint.

rows.organisation_system: NATS (UK air traffic control, flight data system)
rows.what_happened: A software defect corrupted flight data updates at the London Area Control centre, and controllers restricted air traffic to keep it safe.
rows.impact: About 2,000 flights cancelled, days of disruption and hundreds of thousands of passengers affected (Reuters). The transport secretary ordered an independent review by the Civil Aviation Authority.
rows.cause: A software defect in a specific part of the flight data system: a paused request did not resume correctly and its output was corrupted, per NATS's preliminary report.

rows.what_happened: A CVSS 10 file-read vulnerability is being exploited and was added to CISA KEV.
rows.impact: Patched 10 Sep 2026; Censys counted about 86,000 reachable hosts (per Cybernews).
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code.

rows.organisation_system: Spain's data protection agency (first AI-agent breach notice)
rows.what_happened: Spain's data protection agency AEPD received its first breach notice in which an AI agent carried out the attack.
rows.impact: No count given. The agent changed personal data and reached invoices. The AEPD has not verified the case.
rows.cause: An AI agent searched for weaknesses, logged in and used a flaw in the application.

rows.what_happened: Attackers compromised two third-party security appliances with zero-day exploits, reached the exchange's wallet environment and made unauthorised transfers from its hot and warm wallets over nearly three hours.
rows.impact: USD 387.5 million in crypto stolen across several blockchains. Bitget's chief executive blamed North Korean hackers.
rows.cause: Zero-day flaws in third-party security products, per investigations by SlowMist and Mandiant that Bitget cited.

rows.what_happened: Researchers found a publicly accessible database holding SMS messages sent by banks, airlines and others; it could still be read as new messages were added.
rows.impact: More than 125 million SMS messages dated from 20 Oct 2022 to September 2026.
rows.cause: An exposed ClickHouse database. The company acknowledged a security vulnerability in one of its systems and said it is fixed.

rows.what_happened: A third party got unauthorised access to a system the furniture retailer manages.
rows.impact: Up to 37.62 million records of personal information. The attacker likely had access since mid-October; Nitori confirmed the access on 6 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: A third party got unauthorised access to a third-party cloud service the company used.
rows.impact: Personal information of about 7.7 million people: up to 5.8 million members and former members and 1.9 million non-members. First notice 29 Oct 2026; the figure was reported 8 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Unauthorised access to a third-party cloud service.

rows.what_happened: Attackers got into the company's systems and internal tools. Chainalysis described the method as 'offensive agentic techniques'.
rows.impact: First disclosure: customers' names, email addresses, user IDs and role labels. A later update: names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens of all Chainalysis users were exposed.
rows.cause: Attackers using AI tools, in the company's description; the entry point is not stated.

rows.what_happened: A third party got unauthorised access to the system that manages app member information between 2 and 7 Oct 2026.
rows.impact: A server holding 11.18 million customer records. The company determined it on 13 Oct 2026.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: Wellington IT (IT provider to Irish credit unions)
rows.what_happened: A reported cyberattack on the Belfast IT supplier between 2 and 4 Oct 2026 exposed information of credit union members. The company has not publicly disclosed an incident.
rows.impact: About 50 credit unions, 43 of them in Ireland; as many as 1.8 million people could be affected (Irish Times). Reported 17-18 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: An automated script made five million requests to exploit an authorisation flaw in the company's infrastructure, as reported.

rows.organisation_system: Artex AI agent campaigns observed by Amazon
rows.what_happened: Amazon's network of decoy sensors captured requests from AI agents that carried the working memory of offensive campaigns run on Artex, an open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework.
rows.impact: 3 Oct to 5 Nov 2026; published 13 Nov 2026. The most prominent campaign was a large-scale theft of credentials to access AI models; another targeted cryptocurrency exchanges to bypass identity checks with real-time deepfake injection. Amazon cannot verify the outcomes the agents reported.
rows.cause: AI agents ran the campaigns: planner, worker, verification and compression agents sharing one knowledge graph.

rows.organisation_system: Uber via Fireworks AI (third-party AI infrastructure provider)
rows.what_happened: An unauthorised party used valid credentials of a third-party provider to access Uber data in the cloud: driver's licence images and extracted text, names, mailing addresses, dates of birth and licence numbers.
rows.impact: 149,346 people. Uber learned of it 9 Oct and determined the access 13 Oct; notices from 10 Nov 2026. Alerts were enabled but none triggered, because valid credentials were used.
rows.cause: Compromised third-party credentials and permitted data connections. Uber's filings do not name the vendor; an Uber spokesperson named Fireworks AI to TechCrunch.

rows.what_happened: Card skimmer code injected into Fandango's checkout page took payment card details that customers entered from 8 to 11 Oct 2026.
rows.impact: The company has not shared the number of customers. It determined the impact on 30 Oct 2026.
rows.cause: Malicious code injected into the checkout page.

rows.organisation_system: Google Chrome (XBOW full-chain exploit built with AI agents)
rows.what_happened: XBOW chained three then-unknown Chrome bugs into one attack that runs code on a Windows computer when the user only loads a web page. Its researchers built it in six days by directing AI agents on a publicly available OpenAI model.
rows.impact: Google confirmed and fixed all three bugs in Chrome 152 and paid XBOW its top USD 250,000 reward for a full Chrome exploit.
rows.cause: Flaws in the product code. The agents searched the source, built proofs of concept and drafted the exploit; the researchers chose the targets and decided which pieces to join.
