rows.what_happened: A threat actor used IAM credentials from an AWS account associated with Qubole to assume the IAM roles that customers had created to trust Qubole, then collected configuration, secrets and S3 data in victim environments.
rows.impact: Multiple Qubole customers; no count given. Activity seen 14 to 26 Oct 2026; published by Wiz on 9 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Abuse of the cross-account access customers grant to a vendor. Qubole had not posted a statement when The Hacker News checked.

rows.organisation_system: Check Point Security Management servers (22 organisations)
rows.what_happened: A campaign that GreyNoise tracks as GT13 compromised 24 Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organisations. Confirmed activity ran from October 17 to November 2, 2026, and the actor used one HFS server to pull data from the compromised servers.
rows.impact: 22 organisations (BleepingComputer: spread across 17 countries); 24 Security Management servers; over 100 management tasks run on the servers; 99 IP addresses used. Data exfiltration from 24 previously compromised servers (THN).
rows.cause: Check Point says the attackers used CVE-2026-16232, a SmartConsole authentication bypass it disclosed in July 2026. GreyNoise assesses that the actor ran an AI-powered offensive tool, based on behaviour, automation and custom tooling; AI use is unconfirmed.

rows.what_happened: A third party got unauthorised access to part of the account opening system that an external contractor runs for the broker.
rows.impact: Up to 1.13 million email addresses and 1,592 identity document images. The contractor confirmed an access attempt on 18 Oct; Monex announced it on 13 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Unauthorised access at an external contractor.

rows.what_happened: An attacker exploited a previously unknown vulnerability in Railway's build infrastructure, moved across internal systems and decrypted a subset of customer variables. Railway believes the attacker was after AI provider credentials.
rows.impact: At most 1.85% (about 100,000) of workspaces; linked-account tokens of 1,852 users; unauthorised spend on the stolen keys estimated at about $740,000. 07:28 UTC 20 Oct to 09:24 UTC 21 Oct 2026; report published 10 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: A flaw in the multi-tenant build infrastructure let the attacker read files on the host. Railway, citing Wiz, says it was defending against abliterated models and a harness similar to ARTEX.

rows.what_happened: Two critical flaws in the PHP runtime let an unauthenticated attacker crash it, read memory or run code with crafted HTTP traffic; every web server running PHP 5.4 (2012) or later was affected.
rows.impact: Fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 21 Oct 2026. Cloudflare saw attack traffic; CISA added both to KEV on 26 Oct 2026.
rows.cause: Memory handling when a request fails unexpectedly, including when memory runs out. Calif.io, Wiz, OpenAI and Quarkslab disclosed them; Wiz says AI found them.

rows.what_happened: LiteLLM's release pipeline was compromised and pushed version 1.107.0 to PyPI and the Docker registry with compiled malware that steals credentials and loads remote code execution tools.
rows.impact: The PyPI release was live for about two hours and the Docker images for about two and a half; earlier versions were safe and the releases were pulled.
rows.cause: An administrative key committed to a public repository in May 2026 and a GitHub token of an organisation owner; the attacker overrode branch protection and built from a lookalike fork, per LiteLLM.

rows.what_happened: The Commission confirmed a cyberattack that its spokesperson described as an 'AI-generated cyber campaign' involving a publicly available AI tool.
rows.impact: First signs detected 22 Oct 2026; confirmed 19 Nov 2026. Personnel systems, including payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements and translation services, were reportedly disrupted for more than 10 days. On 23 Nov 2026 the Commission confirmed that the attackers also breached the EU Academy learning platform and leaked the names and email addresses of its users.
rows.cause: A publicly available AI tool that the Commission did not name. Politico reported that CERT-EU identified it as ARTEX.

rows.what_happened: A cyberattack disrupted GlobeTopper's B2B gift card platform. The parent iQSTEL says the intrusion was detected on October 22, the platform was suspended and taken offline on October 23, and a rebuilt platform went live on AWS on October 31, with commercial operations restored in stages from November 1. Attackers redeemed digital gift cards worth about $70,000 that cannot be recovered. They also obtained some business customers' API credentials and integration keys, which have been revoked and replaced.
rows.impact: BleepingComputer reports an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue. About $70,000 of gift cards redeemed. iQSTEL says the incident hurt fourth-quarter transaction volume but has not determined it to be material.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: An unauthorised party got into Fireworks development machines hosted at a third-party cloud provider that had its own security incident, and used that access to reach part of the production systems.
rows.impact: 23 to 30 Oct 2026. Account and billing information for all accounts created before 30 Oct; datasets, models or secrets for a small number of customers. An earlier intrusion ran from 3 Aug to 7 Oct 2026.
rows.cause: Access through a third-party cloud provider. Fireworks links the evidence to a financially motivated group that sells stolen access to large language models ('LLMJacking').

rows.what_happened: The breach at Fireworks AI, Notion's AI infrastructure provider, exposed Notion AI chat transcripts in a small number of workspaces.
rows.impact: Less than 1% of Notion users, per the company. Fireworks alerted Notion on 2 Nov; Notion disclosed it on 11 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: The vendor's breach. Fireworks had contractually committed to zero data retention for Notion data, per Notion.

rows.organisation_system: Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux (five attack chains from Anthropic's research)
rows.what_happened: Anthropic published five attack chains found with an unreleased research model: one-click code execution in Chrome, a one-click chain in Safari, an Android lock screen bypass, a remote denial of service in Windows and zero-click code execution in Linux (CVE-2026-98432).
rows.impact: 62 CVEs assigned and patched in Chrome, all rated critical or high. The kernel's CVE team rates the Linux flaw 9.8.
rows.cause: Flaws in the product code, found and chained into exploits by an Anthropic AI model.

rows.what_happened: Attackers used an internal wallet signing service to send transactions outside the normal withdrawal process. Binance traced the path to fake job interviews, a trojanised installer on an engineer's machine and abuse of an internal AI tool.
rows.impact: About USD 6.43 billion in assets stolen, by Binance's count; the FBI attributed the theft of more than USD 6 billion to North Korea's TraderTraitor.
rows.cause: Social engineering of wallet engineers and stolen credentials; an internal AI tool was abused to gain control over two more engineers, per Binance.

rows.what_happened: Attackers distributed malicious versions of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace. The malware installed persistent SSH backdoors.
rows.impact: Up to 5,000 developers exposed; the malicious versions were available for about 11 hours. Cursor published its incident report on 13 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: The attackers obtained an access key stored on Fireworks AI, per Cursor.

rows.what_happened: Maersk confirmed that a threat actor breached its systems after the WhiteArmor ransomware group claimed the attack and demanded $5 million. Reported 11 Nov 2026.
rows.impact: Maersk: the incident is isolated to a local system and no sensitive data has been disclosed.
rows.cause: A ransomware attack claimed by WhiteArmor; the method is not stated.

rows.organisation_system: SBC Medical Group Holdings (clinics in Japan)
rows.what_happened: Hackers accessed an online platform the company manages and compromised databases holding customer information of clinics in Japan.
rows.impact: Over 2 million individuals; the basic information of 1,624,000 people was stolen, per the company's SEC filing as reported on 20 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: ARARA email service (SEGA among nearly 380 clients)
rows.what_happened: ARARA disclosed on 2 Nov 2026 a breach of its email distribution service. SEGA said the email addresses of its newsletter subscribers were exposed.
rows.impact: 77 million email addresses from nearly 380 corporate clients; 2.2 million of them SEGA newsletter subscribers.
rows.cause: A web server vulnerability and problems in the system environment, per ARARA; the exact method is under investigation.

rows.what_happened: A hack drained funds from the crypto exchange's hot wallets.
rows.impact: The exchange will absorb a $40 million loss; Chainalysis estimated about $49 million drained across 17 blockchains. Only hot wallets were hit, the exchange said.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: Barracuda Email Security Gateway and other products (CVE-2026-116606, CVE-2026-111560)
rows.what_happened: Barracuda published an advisory for a pre-authentication authorisation bypass and a command injection that together could give an attacker root access to the device.
rows.impact: Exploitation affecting a small number of organisations, per Barracuda. CISA added both to its exploited list on 10 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Flaws in the product code.

rows.organisation_system: Linux kernel (948 privilege escalation flaws from OpenAI's pipeline)
rows.what_happened: OpenAI described an autonomous pipeline that finds, exploits and patches vulnerabilities. In one run over the Linux kernel it produced working local privilege escalation exploits and patches for 948 flaws; OpenAI researchers reviewed the output and reported the flaws with the patches.
rows.impact: 2,308 candidate findings analysed, 1,724 reproduced, 948 exploited and patched, for about USD 1.2 million of API cost, per OpenAI.
rows.cause: AI analysis, with OpenAI researchers.

rows.what_happened: Cleverbridge detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026 and took systems offline; they were brought back the same day. Its investigation found that a third party copied payment card data stored on its platform. Customers began receiving notices on November 20.
rows.impact: Number of customers affected was not disclosed. The customer notice (as shown to BleepingComputer) lists card number, expiry date and CVV/CVC; name and billing details were reportedly not copied.
rows.cause: Not stated. Cleverbridge has not said how attackers got in or how long they stayed.

rows.what_happened: 5G SA subscribers nationwide had trouble with voice calls, data and SMS three times: from about 11:18 JST on 5 Nov 2026, from 10:34 JST on 11 Nov, and from 10:02 to 15:58 JST on 16 Nov.
rows.impact: Nationwide, 5G SA subscribers only; emergency calls were not affected.
rows.cause: 16 Nov: traffic concentrated on the switching equipment that serves 5G SA customers, per Docomo. The earlier notices give the cause as under investigation, with no sign of unauthorised access or cyberattack.

rows.what_happened: A flaw let remote attackers log in to passwordless accounts on Alpine Linux and other musl-based systems that do not check passwords through PAM. Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 on 5 Nov 2026.
rows.impact: The first attack attempt came less than nine hours after the CVE was published, with root access confirmed on a honeypot (Previdian). CISA added it to its exploited list on 9 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code. The finder said he worked with swarms of AI agents.

rows.what_happened: A crafted SOAP fault message makes Axis 1.x, which is past end of life, create a class the attacker names.
rows.impact: CISA added it to its exploited list on 18 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Unsafe reflection in the product code.

rows.organisation_system: TSMC (employee data at a cloud provider)
rows.what_happened: A threat actor leaked a sample of TSMC employee data on a hacker forum on 8 Nov 2026 and put the rest up for auction. TSMC confirmed that data of current and former employees was made available without authorisation.
rows.impact: The actor claimed 6.9GB with 46,000 employee records. TSMC found no evidence that its own systems were compromised.
rows.cause: The leaked data matched data stored at a cloud service provider TSMC uses, per the company.

rows.what_happened: Google fixed a use-after-free flaw in Chrome's XML component and said an exploit for it exists in the wild.
rows.impact: The eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks in 2026, per BleepingComputer. CISA added it to its exploited list on 10 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code.

rows.what_happened: A spoofing flaw in Outlook leaked a user's NTLMv2 hash when a crafted Office file was opened; Microsoft says it was exploited in the wild as a zero-day.
rows.impact: Fixed in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday, which addressed 1,093 CVEs (Tenable count). Rated moderate, CVSS 6.5.
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code. Microsoft's advisory credits a security researcher who used an Anthropic model.

rows.organisation_system: SAP NetWeaver, Web Dispatcher and Gateway (four CVSS 10.0 flaws)
rows.what_happened: SAP's November 2026 security updates fixed 35 vulnerabilities, four of them rated 10 out of 10: CVE-2026-76964, CVE-2026-89126, CVE-2026-89103 and CVE-2026-120017.
rows.impact: Rated 10/10 by SAP; exploitation needs no SAP user, no password and no user interaction.
rows.cause: Flaws in the product code, among them memory corruption and missing authentication.

rows.what_happened: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 has a bypass of its -dSAFER sandbox that allows arbitrary code execution.
rows.impact: Made public on 10 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: A procedure calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking operand types.

rows.what_happened: An authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra and XOA lets a remote attacker with network access to the management interface log in without credentials, via a crafted cookie containing an empty JSON object. Vates confirms the flaw is actively exploited by a threat actor. The attacker can list reusable login token IDs through a REST API endpoint; Vates warns this can lead to admin actions, code execution on managed pools and full root takeover of XCP-ng nodes.
rows.impact: Not stated numerically. Admin-level control of managed pools and root on XCP-ng nodes are the potential outcomes per Vates.
rows.cause: Authentication bypass in cookie processing: a crafted cookie with an empty JSON object makes the platform retrieve an existing token and log the attacker in as its owner. Discovered by Filip Magic and Christoffer Olsen of TDC NET Security (per BleepingComputer).

rows.organisation_system: Linux kernel (59 reports from Microsoft's MDASH)
rows.what_happened: Microsoft's AI system MDASH found Linux kernel flaws that led to 59 public upstream reports and 33 CVEs.
rows.impact: Working root exploits confirmed for eight of the CVEs. The oldest, a cls_u32 bug (CVE-2026-74544), had been there for at least 21 years.
rows.cause: AI analysis, with Microsoft researchers.

rows.what_happened: Actions workflow starts were delayed or failed, webhook requests failed, Pages deployments did not complete and Copilot features were partly unavailable.
rows.impact: 20:05 to 21:02 UTC on 11 Nov 2026. About 3.4 million partially created Actions runs were cancelled; about 63% of webhook API requests failed in the Central US stamp.
rows.cause: An Azure Cosmos DB regional outage: a configuration change to the Central US gateways exposed a latent race condition under a specific high-load traffic pattern.

rows.what_happened: An outage of logins, sign-ups, work mode, dots, sites and spaces, with elevated error rates when creating conversations through the API.
rows.impact: 20:43 to 20:52 UTC on 11 Nov 2026 (about nine minutes), per the status page.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Lock contention in a July fix for Microsoft 365 gateway servers exhausted server resources; Teams traffic had been moved to the same gateway.
rows.impact: 16:20 UTC 12 Nov to 16:10 UTC 13 Nov (23 hours 50 minutes); over 80% of servers unresponsive at the low point (preliminary PIR).
rows.cause: Latent defect; about 14% of servers already out from an unrelated issue. Microsoft's final status: 'not related to cyber or AI/agents'.

rows.what_happened: A flood of connections on the legacy FTI network forced a nationwide ground stop.
rows.impact: Problem from about 20:30 UTC (about 3:30 p.m. ET); ground stop ended 01:15 UTC 14 Nov (8:15 p.m. ET); 17 of 22 control centres affected; about 3,500 aircraft landed.
rows.cause: New router installed by L3Harris, the FAA's network service provider, at the El Dorado site. FAA says the SMART system is not related.

rows.organisation_system: Workday (WD1; WD5 in later customer reports)
rows.what_happened: While validating the disaster-recovery maintenance window, DR tenants unexpectedly connected to production databases.
rows.impact: Restored by 16:00 UTC 14 Nov (11:00 a.m. EST) per a Workday spokesperson; some customers took longer. Workday says two data centres were hit, not a cyber incident.
rows.cause: Isolation between disaster-recovery and production failed; no root-cause analysis published yet.

rows.what_happened: Users could not authenticate to claude.ai and Claude Code; the status page lists elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code and platform.claude.com.
rows.impact: 09:58 to 11:58 UTC on 13 Nov 2026, per the status page.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: A cybercriminal accessed one of LaLiga's technology platforms for fan services and extracted personal data of users registered for LaLiga and some clubs' digital services. LaLiga's security team blocked the attacker and stopped the extraction on November 16. LaLiga reported it to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and filed a complaint with the National Police cybercrime unit.
rows.impact: Number of users affected was not disclosed. No ransomware group had claimed it at publication. LaLiga did not reply on which clubs were affected.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Sign-up errors, authentication issues and connectivity issues in the US-EAST-1 Region. Customers who sign in through IAM Identity Center to the AWS Console or to services such as Kiro and Connect were affected.
rows.impact: 3:05 AM to 6:10 AM PST on 15 Nov 2026 (about three hours). AWS said there were no workarounds for impacted customers.
rows.cause: Not stated in the AWS event log.

rows.what_happened: Accenture found attackers exploiting MiCollab flaws before Mitel's advisory. A web shell was deployed on November 15; commands ran on one MiCollab server 12 minutes after the first request, and root access followed within half an hour. About 20 hours after the first request, the attackers reached internal backup and database servers. Accenture's Apex Labs did not link the activity to a known group and thinks it may have been an extortion effort. Accenture says some of the malicious activity may have been driven by AI tools.
rows.impact: One MiCollab server taken to root; internal backup and database servers reached. A second victim's MiCollab server had been in contact with the same attacker infrastructure since November 9; how it was compromised is unknown.

rows.what_happened: Some customer transactions were slow or held up, including online banking, Zelle and in-branch; customers could still access their accounts.
rows.impact: No official duration. User reports from about 16:30 UTC (11:30 a.m. ET); the bank said transactions were posting normally by 23:30 UTC (6:30 p.m. ET).
rows.cause: A software bug in on-premise hardware systems; the bank said there was no evidence it was cyber-related.

rows.what_happened: GTIG found an exposed staging server running an autonomous framework that compared patches, drafted exploits and ran them without human intervention.
rows.impact: Targets were French media, entertainment and education websites. GTIG: first time it saw threat actors fully automate discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop.
rows.cause: Misuse of agentic LLM frameworks; the target class was patched (n-day) vulnerabilities.

rows.what_happened: Malicious code was injected into customer JavaScript snippets served by Optimizely: a card skimmer, crypto address swapping and iOS exploit delivery.
rows.impact: 188 snippets at 178 organisations (Report URI count, likely higher); about $7,000 in crypto taken; successful device infection not proven.
rows.cause: Flaw in Optimizely's account signup flow. A Content Security Policy blocked the payload on 24 of 256 hosts checked (15%).

rows.what_happened: A system outage forced United to delay departing flights. Pilots told air traffic controllers that the problem was in a system that helps them determine a plane's final weight.
rows.impact: More than 90 minutes; resolved about one hour and 40 minutes after pilots first reported problems.
rows.cause: Not stated. United said there was no indication of a cybersecurity issue.

rows.what_happened: A cyberattack disrupted N-able services from 16 Nov 2026; the company confirmed on 18 Nov that an attack was behind the disruption.
rows.impact: N-able says the incident was isolated to a single web server.
rows.cause: A cyberattack; the method is not stated.

rows.what_happened: TfL discovered a security incident on 16 Nov 2026 that may have exposed the account details of Oyster photocard customers. Customers had reported emails asking them to create an account; the emails came directly from TfL's mail systems as a result of a compromise.
rows.impact: Around 265,000 customers.
rows.cause: A compromise of TfL's mail systems; the method is not stated.

rows.what_happened: Infoblox confirmed unauthorised access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.
rows.impact: The company would not say how many customers were affected.
rows.cause: A compromised vendor.

rows.organisation_system: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard (third-party vendors)
rows.what_happened: JPMorgan said third parties that provide services to the firm were the target of a cyberattack; Visa and Mastercard each pointed to an incident at a third-party provider. An extortion group calling itself n0n posted its claims on 16 Nov 2026.
rows.impact: Marketing data that may include customer names and email addresses, per JPMorgan. The posted data appears to hold more than 16,000 customer email addresses (Reuters review, not verified). Visa: no payments data such as card numbers were affected.
rows.cause: Attacks on service providers; the vendors are not named.

rows.what_happened: CNN reported that the highly classified NSA network (NSA Net) was down or intermittent.
rows.impact: Duration not known; CNN reports no evidence of a cyberattack. No official statement found as of 17 Nov.
rows.cause: Unknown; CBS sources cite routine system patching.

rows.what_happened: An out-of-bounds write in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder could let an unauthenticated attacker take over a Java server before the application can reject the input.
rows.impact: Oracle shipped fixed Java SE builds on 17 Nov 2026; CVSS 4.0 9.2 per Calif. No exploitation reported at disclosure. Early reports name OpenJDK 17.0.6 (January 2023) and later as affected.
rows.cause: Memory corruption in the Java runtime itself. Calif's Quang Luong found it in about an hour auditing OpenJDK with an OpenAI coding agent, for under $200 in compute.

rows.what_happened: Apple Music, the App Store and AppleCare suffered full outages, and the iCloud sign-in interface had issues, per Apple's status page.
rows.impact: Duration not stated; Apple said the same day that many of its systems were back up.
rows.cause: An internal update, per Apple's statement.

rows.organisation_system: Panama power system (Gatun plant, Ensa and Naturgy customers)
rows.what_happened: A trip of unit G2 at the Gatun thermoelectric plant cut power to customers of Ensa and Naturgy in the early hours of 17 Nov 2026.
rows.impact: 192,238 Ensa customers were without power; over 307,000 customers in all for up to 13 minutes (Rio Times).
rows.cause: The loss of about 295 MW of generation when the unit tripped. The sources name no computer fault.

rows.what_happened: Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 deserialise untrusted data, which lets an unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary code.
rows.impact: Actively exploited, per Apache. CISA added it to its exploited list on 20 Nov 2026.
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code.

rows.organisation_system: Bell Canada (circuit ordering and provisioning system)
rows.what_happened: Bell confirmed that an agentic threat actor accessed some of its systems on November 17, 2026, including a system used for ordering and provisioning circuits, and took some enterprise customer data. The customer notice says the data is business contact details, ticket titles and some IP addresses, with no credentials.
rows.impact: Bell has not disclosed how many enterprise customers were affected or how much data was stolen. Bell says there was no impact to customer services.
rows.cause: An attacker Bell calls an 'agentic threat actor'. Bell does not say how it got in.

rows.what_happened: Attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of the Rackspace Spot platform on November 17, 2026 (about 00:20 to 22:00 UTC). They could create pods in customer clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes. The admin console was taken down for an extended outage and restored on November 21. On November 24 Rackspace announced it will shut the service down permanently on December 8, 2026.
rows.impact: Customers' cluster Secrets (any Secret in an affected cluster), Spot API tokens and refresh tokens may have been read. Number of customers and whether customer data was stolen were not disclosed.
rows.cause: Leaked (compromised) credentials, per the Rackspace customer notice.

rows.what_happened: Equinor detected an ongoing cyber-attack against certain IT systems on November 17. Production was unaffected. On November 19 it said the attack did not appear to be specifically targeting Equinor and it had reported the matter to police. On November 20 it said the attack had been stopped.
rows.impact: Production unaffected. Equinor: 'no indication that data has been stolen or altered.' Affected systems not named. No negative consequences for employees, partners or suppliers, per Equinor.
rows.cause: Not stated. Equinor's page does not name a vector and does not mention Azure or an API.

rows.what_happened: Two critical flaws in nginx's HTTP/2 code let an unauthenticated attacker run code on the server; CVE-2026-123007 had been in every release since 1.9.5 (September 2015). Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 and Xint found them independently.
rows.impact: CVSS 4.0 9.2; F5 fixed them with three more critical flaws in nginx 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 on 18 Nov 2026. No attacks reported at disclosure; a public proof of concept exists.
rows.cause: Integer underflow in HTTP/2 flow-control accounting (CVE-2026-123007) and a use-after-free (CVE-2026-123633). Wiz says its AI code-scanning harness found both.

rows.what_happened: A one-byte heap overflow in Ruby's string case conversion is reachable without authentication in common Ruby web frameworks, Rails and classic Sinatra apps by default.
rows.impact: Fixed in Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 with six more advisories; Ruby says proofs of concept show some of them can lead to remote code execution. Every release back to 2.4.0 (December 2016) carries the bug.
rows.cause: The same conversion loop in several ISO-8859 and Windows-125x encodings. The Ruby advisory credits Stephan Lipp (Ada Logics) and Anthropic; Veria Labs found it independently.

rows.organisation_system: Microsoft Azure API Management Classic tiers
rows.what_happened: A flaw in Azure API Management Classic was exploited to steal stored secrets: Named Values, client secrets for identity and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys and tokens for direct management APIs. Microsoft identified the issue on November 18, deployed a mitigation on November 19 and closed the unauthorized access path. Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) says an unknown threat actor targeted these stored items, and BleepingComputer reports that the flaw has been linked to attacks on Norwegian organisations, including energy companies.
rows.impact: Stored secrets exposed to the attacker; Microsoft says it 'does not automatically invalidate credentials that may have been accessed before the fix was deployed.' Consumption tier and all v2 tiers not affected. No customer counts given.
rows.cause: Vulnerability in APIM Classic tiers; no CVE id given in the article.

rows.organisation_system: PHP (phpAfterShell, CVE-2026-126714, and six more critical flaws)
rows.what_happened: PHP fixed 17 security flaws, seven of them critical; phpAfterShell, in the default file-based session handler, can let a remote attacker run code on the server.
rows.impact: Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 on 19 Nov 2026. PHP says the critical issues need non-default configuration or uncommon setups; none was in CISA KEV on 19 Nov.
rows.cause: An interrupted session write leaves a mix of new and old data that the next request deserializes. depthfirst says its AI models, working with its researchers, found it.

rows.what_happened: An authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service let an unauthenticated attacker with network access take administrative control of vCenter.
rows.impact: Exploited since early September 2026; Broadcom patched it on 19 Nov 2026 in VMSA-2026-0009 without confirming the attacks itself.
rows.cause: Flaw in the product code. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence attribute the attacks to Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221), a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group.

rows.what_happened: An unauthorized party accessed an internal-only Cloud WAF management API that was reachable from the public internet with no authentication. The attacker could reach customer contact details and, for some customers, the credentials used to export WAF logs to their own storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage or SFTP). Radware blocked the IP, revoked and replaced internal credentials, and detected the access about ten hours after it began.
rows.impact: Customer contact details and, for a subset of customers, log-export credentials potentially accessed. Radware says there is no evidence of changes to customer security policies or of access to application traffic, and that WAF protection continued. Customers reported AWS alerts for an unfamiliar IP address accessing their log buckets. Number of customers affected was not disclosed.
rows.cause: The internal Cloud WAF management API was exposed to the public internet without authentication (per Radware's root cause analysis).

rows.what_happened: Under specific conditions an attacker could use the Drupal installer to reinstall the site, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution. Drupal's Security Team received a report that it was exploited on live sites from 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC. CISA added it to KEV on November 24 (per SecurityWeek).
rows.impact: SecurityWeek: 'It's unclear how many websites are affected.' Drupal says some but not all exploit paths are mitigated if settings.php cannot be written. Count not given.
rows.cause: Installer reinstall condition. Drupal: 'Under specific conditions, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal.'

rows.what_happened: An attacker used a compromised employee corporate GitHub account to reach private repositories, pushed malicious code to backend services, and downloaded administrative data about customers. 1Password says customer vaults were not accessed.
rows.impact: Account records for a subset of users (names, email addresses, account and user IDs, creation and last sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters); invitation, provisioning and account-recovery tokens for a small number of users; internal source code copied. No exact count given. 1Password found no internal evidence of customer account takeovers.
rows.cause: Compromised employee corporate GitHub account, used to push malicious code to backend services.

rows.what_happened: Cloudflare's status history lists network performance issues in its Washington, DC datacenter (IAD).
rows.impact: 20:35 UTC 20 Nov to 07:44 UTC 21 Nov 2026 (about 11 hours), rated minor.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Apparent hackers reportedly breached the NCIC, the nationwide database police use to share warrants, missing-person and background-check information. The FBI has not confirmed it, and it is unclear when the breach happened, how access was gained, or whether data was stolen.
rows.impact: Not stated. Unclear whether sensitive records were accessed or whether availability was affected.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Microsoft says attackers exploited a flaw in the Entra Connect Health API to get unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level metadata, including administrator and technical contact email addresses. Microsoft found the flaw on November 9, 2026, fixed it on November 19 and concluded its investigation on November 20.
rows.impact: Microsoft has not said how many organisations or tenants were affected. More than a dozen administrators have posted that they received the notice. Exposed: admin and technical contact emails, tenant IDs, display names, domains, license tiers, sync status and an expired certificate. Microsoft says no passwords, hashes, tokens or keys were exposed.
rows.cause: A vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API, first introduced July 23, 2026 (per the Microsoft notice as reported by BleepingComputer).

rows.what_happened: An unauthorized party exploited a flaw in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service and installed malware on some routers and KVM devices; some users found backdoors and root reverse shells. GL.iNet blocked the attack path on November 20 and says devices can no longer be newly infected through it. Security firmware removes the known malware.
rows.impact: Number of devices and customers affected was not disclosed. Unknown whether data was stolen from devices or whether computers behind infected KVM devices were compromised. RemoteToHome reports that most of nearly 200 routers it checked appeared affected, by this attack or an older backdoor dating to September 2025.
rows.cause: Not stated by GL.iNet. RemoteToHome's code analysis says GoodCloud ran commands from cloud messages without checking them; GL.iNet has not confirmed this.

rows.organisation_system: KEPCO, Korea Electric Power Corporation (billing and procurement systems)
rows.what_happened: A threat actor breached KEPCO's internal network and accessed two systems: the KEPCO ON electricity billing platform and the SRM procurement system. KEPCO confirmed unauthorized access on November 20, blocked external IP addresses and suspended the affected services. A hacker using the alias Noiem claimed the attack on a forum on November 19; BleepingComputer says attribution is unconfirmed.
rows.impact: 1,520,248 people in total per the company breakdown as transcribed by BleepingComputer: 650,487 KEPCO ON customers (names, ID information, phone numbers, addresses, bank account and card details, billing data); 426,827 company representatives (names, ID information, emails, company addresses); 442,934 KEPCO employees (names, affiliation, employee ID, phone and email).
rows.cause: The company says the breach resulted from 'advanced technologies such as AI', with no detail on the initial access method or attack chain.

rows.what_happened: Third parties accessed a database holding information on users of McDonald's Japan's official app. The exposed information is product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data and internal customer management IDs. The company says no service disruption or misuse of the app was found.
rows.impact: Number of people affected and detection date were not disclosed. The company says names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses and credit card information were not included.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: US Department of Agriculture (farm loan, payment and mapping systems)
rows.what_happened: USDA's Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center detected a security incident, and on 16 November staff were told to reset database passwords across all environments, which meant restarting the applications. Farm Service Agency loan software, the Natural Resources Conservation Service ProTracts payment system and mapping software went offline for several days. On 20 November Under Secretary Richard Fordyce confirmed it was a cyber threat, not a software update, and said no personally identifiable information was involved and no data was lost. NBC News, citing two former department officials, reported that hackers had accessed the system used to pay farmers; USDA has not confirmed this.
rows.impact: Multi-day outages of farmer-facing loan, payment and mapping applications ahead of the 11 December enrollment deadline for the 2026 ARC and PLC programs. USDA says no data was lost.
rows.cause: Not stated: USDA has not said who was behind the intrusion or how it happened.

rows.what_happened: Turnitin disclosed that it recently identified unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems. It activated its incident response plan, brought in outside cybersecurity specialists and notified law enforcement and regulators. The company says its systems are fully operational and safe to use.
rows.impact: Not disclosed. Turnitin has not said whether any data was accessed or stolen, when the activity happened, or how many people were affected. It says the affected systems do not collect government ID credentials or institutional financial information. University of Colorado Boulder said it had no indication its data was exposed.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: OpenRouter (three AI providers removed over leaked prompts and secrets)
rows.what_happened: OpenRouter removed three AI providers after a Dragos study found data from at least three AI providers was exposed. Dragos sent about two million seeded prompts containing canary URLs and credentials, and the seeded prompts were used in attempts to reach Dragos test systems and canary AWS accounts. Some leaked credentials were used in the wild. OpenRouter revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints as a precaution.
rows.impact: Prompts and secrets (credentials) exposed; ZDR revoked for 125 endpoints; affected users advised to rotate secrets. No user or request count given.
rows.cause: Provider-side: OpenRouter says there was no breach of its own systems and places the leak at the provider level. Together AI says OpenRouter had not turned on ZDR for its traffic (its own characterisation). Atlas Cloud withdrew models after a third-party incident.

rows.what_happened: Zodia detected attempts to probe its platform on 23 November, took its B2B API offline as a precaution, and found unauthorised access the next day. Limited client information was accessed. Zodia says there were no unauthorised transactions.
rows.impact: Limited client information (publicly available details about client organisations); for a small number of clients and employees, a business contact name and email address. No unauthorised transactions found so far. The B2B API was restored after added security measures.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Requests to several Claude models returned elevated errors. Anthropic identified the cause, deployed a fix, and then resolved the incident.
rows.impact: Anthropic rated it major in its status feed. The page lists most current Claude models as affected. No user counts given. Status updates ran from 09:49 to 11:07 UTC.
rows.cause: Not described. Anthropic says only that the cause was identified.

rows.what_happened: Unknown attackers reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the CIA, according to a source and The New York Times. The NYT reported the attack used the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. The CIA and ODNI did not reply to requests for details. A source says no classified systems or information were involved.
rows.impact: Not stated. Sources say no classified data or systems were exposed. Scope of data taken is not known.
rows.cause: Reportedly the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework was used (NYT, as relayed by BleepingComputer).

rows.what_happened: Spotify users reported a sudden spike of login problems, and the live blog says Spotify fixed the problem in a little over an hour.
rows.impact: Peak of over 15,000 Downdetector reports (user-submitted figure, per Tom's Guide live blog); live blog says about 70% of reports were about getting access to the platform.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: FinCEN said it is investigating a cybersecurity incident that gave unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems, and it took some systems offline as a precaution. It granted temporary filing relief to filers affected by the service disruption.
rows.impact: Limited subset of FinCEN systems; some FinCEN services may be temporarily unavailable. Filing relief reference FIN-2026-R002. No user counts given.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Requests to one Claude model returned elevated errors. Anthropic deployed a fix and then resolved the incident.
rows.impact: Anthropic rated it major in its status feed. Components: claude.ai, Claude API, Claude Code, Claude Cowork. No user counts given. Anthropic gives the impact as 17:09 to 17:27 UTC.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.organisation_system: Critical infrastructure in Italy and Switzerland (CSIRT Italia and NCSC warnings)
rows.what_happened: CSIRT Italia (Italy) and the Swiss National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned of automated attacks run by AI agents against critical infrastructure organisations. CSIRT Italia reports large-scale campaigns in which autonomous agents found and exploited flaws and misconfigurations on exposed endpoints; the NCSC reports its first successful AI-assisted attacks. The article names four AI pentest or red-team frameworks linked to recent incidents: ARTEX AI, CyberStrikeAI, DeepSeek Harness - Red Team, and PentAGI.
rows.impact: NCSC: 'Various organisations and operators of critical infrastructure across at least two sectors have been affected.' No count of victims given.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: A remotely exploitable OS command injection in AutomatedProvisioner lets an attacker run arbitrary commands as root via a crafted Salt minion ID. Juniper's SIRT received a report of at least one malicious exploitation instance. CISA later added the flaw to KEV and told federal agencies to patch within three days under BOD 26-04.
rows.impact: At least one instance of malicious exploitation reported to Juniper SIRT (per SecurityWeek). No victim count given.
rows.cause: OS command injection (CVSS 9.8) in the AutomatedProvisioner service of Session Smart Conductor; patched in 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3 (Session Smart Router and Conductor).

rows.organisation_system: OpenAI (ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex Cloud)
rows.what_happened: Users of ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex Cloud threads saw elevated conversation errors until OpenAI applied mitigations and then reported recovery.
rows.impact: OpenAI status feed impact: minor. Components: Conversations (ChatGPT), ChatGPT Work, Codex Web. Duration 11:48 to 16:12 UTC (4 h 24 min). OpenAI gave no user counts.
rows.cause: Not stated. OpenAI's 13:22 UTC update said the investigation into the underlying cause remained ongoing.

rows.organisation_system: Microsoft Windows (NTLM sign-in after the November updates)
rows.what_happened: Microsoft confirmed that Windows November 2026 security updates can cause authentication failures for some third-party apps and devices that use NTLM, mainly authentication proxies and SSO products. No fix was available at the time of reporting.
rows.impact: Not quantified in the article. Affected: third-party apps and devices using NTLM, including authentication proxy servers, SSO solutions and application packaging solutions.
rows.cause: Microsoft says the cause is a proxy device that does not correctly implement NTLM, for example one that sets NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO but sends an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field. The updates are the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements.

rows.organisation_system: GitHub (Git operations, API, Actions and other services)
rows.what_happened: GitHub reported degraded performance and degraded availability across several products after increased failures caused by high database load. GitHub mitigated it by redistributing database load.
rows.impact: Degraded availability for Git Operations and degraded performance for Actions, Packages, Pull Requests and Webhooks (per status page). GitHub rated it critical in its status feed. No user counts given. From 15:55 to 16:52 UTC.
rows.cause: High database load: 'We are investigating increased failures due to high database load.' Root cause analysis not yet published.

rows.what_happened: Code Completions and Next Edit Suggestions in GitHub Copilot had issues; GitHub applied a mitigation and reported recovery.
rows.impact: Affected service: Code Completions and Next Edit Suggestions. GitHub rated it critical in its status feed. No user counts given. From 00:08 to 01:15 UTC.
rows.cause: Not stated. GitHub says a detailed root cause analysis will be shared later.

rows.what_happened: FIFA said it was the victim of a cyberattack in which hackers gained access to a limited set of personal and business information. It did not say when the attack happened or what exactly was taken. FIFA says it is working with law enforcement. Days earlier, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot it said showed FIFA files and later appeared to claim the hack.
rows.impact: Not stated beyond 'a limited set of personal and business information'. A post the article mentions claims more than 12 GB of internal documents leaked; this is not confirmed.
rows.cause: Not stated.

rows.what_happened: Cloudflare Dashboard and related APIs had issues: requests could fail and errors could be displayed. Cloudflare applied a fix and monitored the results before resolving.
rows.impact: Dashboard and API affected; Cloudflare rated it major in its status feed. No user counts given. From 16:03 to 18:17 UTC.
rows.cause: Not stated on the status page.

rows.what_happened: SAP confirmed it had identified suspicious activity and taken measures to protect its customers, and said its investigation had so far found no evidence of unauthorised access to customer business data. Der Spiegel, citing an insider, reported that attackers stole SAP employees' authentication tokens and used them to copy and alter SAP source code on GitHub; SAP has not confirmed the token theft or the code changes. Handelsblatt reported that SAP restricted access to GitHub, paused automated development workflows and replaced signing keys.
rows.impact: Not stated by SAP beyond no evidence so far of access to customer business data. Per the insider account, SAP source code on GitHub was copied and altered. SAP has not said whether any software release delivered to customers was affected.
rows.cause: Stolen employee authentication tokens, according to an insider quoted by Der Spiegel. Der Spiegel also reported that the attackers may have used AI agents; SAP's statement did not address this.

rows.organisation_system: US Air Force Cloud One (cloud computing platform)
rows.what_happened: Hackers breached the Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters; a US official confirmed the hack to NBC News. The intrusion was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system. One source said the intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. Investigators called in Cyber Command. The Air Force said it does not comment on the security posture of specific networks and systems.
rows.impact: Not known: Reuters could not establish the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data was stolen. Migration of back-office applications to Cloud One was paused, updates to applications already on it were blocked, and some users had their administrator rights revoked.
rows.cause: A software vulnerability used to reach the control plane, according to one source; Reuters could not identify it.
